method: 8 specialist lenses, each finding independently attacked by 2 skeptics instructed to refute; a finding is upheld when at least one skeptic could not refute it

findings.title: Mainnet random word is an unconstrained operator input: the Gelato dedicated sender can choose any outcome or veto any draw
findings.preconditions: Control of the immutable OPERATOR address (Gelato's dedicated msg.sender): Gelato infrastructure itself, a compromise of the Gelato account/task, or any future rotation of that key into hostile hands. FWA acquisitions enabled on 999 with the GelatoVRFCoordinator wired (script/DeployHyperEVMMainnetCore.s.sol:83-94).
findings.scenario: `fulfillRandomness(uint256 randomness, bytes calldata dataWithRound)` authenticates ONLY `msg.sender == OPERATOR` and hash-binds ONLY `dataWithRound` (round, requestId, consumer, callbackGasLimit). The `randomness` argument is never checked against the drand round, against any signature, or against any prior commitment. The delivered word is `derivedWord = keccak256(abi.encode(randomness, address(this), block.chainid, requestId))` — with `randomness` a free 256-bit choice, `derivedWord` ranges over the entire output space. FWA then does `target = randomWord % totalWeight; slot = _selectSlot(target)` (FWA.sol:1656-1660) against a pool that is frozen while `unsettledAcquisitionCount != 0` (withdrawListing reverts WithdrawLocked, FWA.sol:1043), so the word→listing map is fully determined and publicly computable at fulfilment time. Concrete: pool of 100 listings, target listing L occupying weight w of totalWeight W. The operator iterates randomness = 0,1,2,... until `keccak256(abi.encode(r, coordinator, 999, requestId)) % W` falls in L's cumulative range; expected W/w ≈ 100 keccak evaluations, microseconds off-chain. Second lever: the operator can instead withhold delivery until `block.number > meta.wordDeadlineBlock` (requestBlock + selectionTimeoutBlocks = 30) and then fulfil, which drives FWA.sol:1505-1510 to mark the acquisition TimedOut and refund it — a per-draw veto. The existing test `testFuzzWordsAreDomainSeparated` (test/GelatoVRFCoordinator.t.sol:172) fuzzes 512 operator-chosen `randomness` values and only asserts that two requests get different words; it demonstrates rather than refutes the free choice.
findings.impact: Every acquisition's outcome is selectable by one key. A colluding purchaser buys the single highest-backing NFT in the pool for the pool's flat EV-based `acquisitionFee = EV*(1+surcharge)` (the harmonic-mean price, FWA.sol:1222-1224) on every draw, repeatedly, until only the cheapest listings remain. Depositors of high-backing listings are drained first; the loss is a direct transfer of NFT value from depositors to the operator/collusion. Detection is possible post-hoc (RandomnessFulfilled emits `gelatoRandomness` and `round`, auditable against drand quicknet) but prevention is zero and settlement is irreversible. The runbook (DRAND_GELATO_RANDOMNESS_RUNBOOK.md:38) acknowledges the operator/task/Gas Tank as operational dependencies, but its claim that the BLS proof is 'vérifiable hors chaîne et non directement dans l'EVM' is false for the beacon this very repo pins on testnet: drand evmnet (DrandRelayCoordinator.sol:25, chain hash 0x04f1e906..., bls-bn254-unchained-on-g1) is BN254 and IS verifiable with the ecPairing precompile. The project selected the one drand beacon (Gelato's quicknet, BLS12-381, genesis 1692803367 at GelatoVRFCoordinator.sol:22) that cannot be checked in the EVM.
findings.minimalFix: Do not ship a mainnet draw whose only integrity property is operator honesty. Preferred: replace the mainnet source with drand evmnet and verify the BN254 signature on-chain in `fulfillRandomness` against the pinned public key + `H(round)` using the ecPairing precompile, then derive the word from `sha256(signature)` (the derivation DrandRelayCoordinator.sol:165 already uses). If Gelato must be kept for delivery, keep it only as a transport and still verify the beacon on-chain. Minimum compensating controls if neither is done before launch: (a) make operator rotation actually possible (see the no-expiry finding — today a malicious operator can permanently block its own removal), (b) bound value at risk per unit time (cap `weightedBackingTotal` or per-block acquisitions) so a grinding operator cannot drain the pool in one block, and (c) state the trust boundary explicitly in the UI and docs.
findings.regressionTest: Add `testOperatorCanSelectAnyListingByGrindingRandomness`: list 3 NFTs with backings 1/10/100 ether, acquire once, then loop `randomness` from 0 upward computing `keccak256(abi.encode(r, address(coordinator), block.chainid, requestId)) % pool.totalWeight()` until it lands in the 100-ether listing's slot range, fulfil with that value, and assert `pool.acquisitions(requestId).listingId == highBackingListingId`. The test must FAIL once on-chain beacon verification is added (assert `fulfillRandomness` reverts for a forged signature).

refutationNotes.reason: SURVIVES at critical. GelatoVRFCoordinator.sol:140-152 authenticates only msg.sender==OPERATOR and hash-binds only dataWithRound; the `randomness` argument is never bound to the round, a signature, or a commitment, and line 154 derives the word as keccak256(abi.encode(randomness, this, chainid, requestId)) — a free 256-bit preimage search. The economic claim checks out and is in fact understated: FWA.sol:819 sets weight = INVERSE_WEIGHT_NUMERATOR/value and 912 accumulates weightedBackingTotal += weight*value, so acquisitionFee() (1222-1226) is a flat harmonic-mean EV independent of which listing is drawn, while a steered purchaser gets the NFT (keepNFT, 1754) or 85% of that listing's backing (settlementDiscountBps=8500, line 314, payout at 1912). Worked pool of 99x0.1 + 1x100 HYPE: EV=0.101, fee with 30% surcharge = 0.131 HYPE, steered payout 85 HYPE. The outcome is fully determined at fulfilment time: _requireExitUnlocked (FWA.sol:1042-1044) freezes withdrawals/repricing/public activation while unsettledAcquisitionCount!=0, the reserved batch is fixed at request time (1372), and with the mainnet FWA_RANDOMNESS_CALLBACK_GAS_LIMIT=900000 the fast path (1531-1546, MIN_FAST_PATH_CALLBACK_GAS_LIMIT=900_000) settles inside the operator's own transaction — and in any case the operator can simply eth_call-simulate each candidate. Not a disclosed known limit (the disclosure covers 998's missing BLS only), not prevented by code, and reachable by the sole party the design trusts. Two corrections to the write-up, neither changing the verdict: (a) the grind cost is W/w in WEIGHT space, so ~10^5 keccaks for the highest-value listing rather than ~100 — still microseconds; (b) the veto lever does not need a late fulfilment, mere withholding lets any caller drive processAcquisitions to the Expired branch (1559-1564). Per the stated rubric ('randomness manipulable to select a chosen outcome') critical is correct.

SURVIVES. I reconstructed the path end to end and could not break it. src/hyperevm/GelatoVRFCoordinator.sol:140-168 authenticates only `msg.sender == OPERATOR` (141) and hash-binds only `dataWithRound` (151); the `randomness` argument is never checked against the round, a signature, or a commitment, and `derivedWord = keccak256(abi.encode(randomness, address(this), block.chainid, requestId))` (154) is therefore a free choice over the whole 2^256 range. The determinism premise also holds: I confirmed the active pool is frozen for the whole window — `_requireExitUnlocked` gates withdrawListing (FWA.sol:1059) and updateBacking (1113), `activateListings` early-returns while `unsettledAcquisitionCount != 0` (FWA.sol:887-889), `_drainStaging` only runs when the count is 0 (876/1275/1327), and new deposits go to staging — so `target = randomWord % totalWeight` (1657) maps to a listing the operator can compute at fulfilment time, and `_tryProcessCallbackHead` (1531-1546) settles it inside the same transaction. The economics hold: `acquisitionFee()` is EV*(1+surcharge) (1222-1226) while `keepNFT` (1754) delivers the NFT and `acceptDepositorBid` (1764) the backing. The timeout veto is real (1505-1510 with 1559-1568). Two corrections to record, neither of which refutes the finding: (1) this is the inherent, documented Gelato VRF trust model — Gelato's own GelatoVRFConsumerBase derives the word from an identically unconstrained operator-supplied `randomness` — so it is a provider-selection / trust-boundary finding, not a defect introduced by the HyperEVM port, and every delivery is publicly auditable after the fact via the `gelatoRandomness`+`round` fields of RandomnessFulfilled (63-69); (2) the finding's assertion that the runbook's BLS sentence 'is false' misreads it — DRAND_GELATO_RANDOMNESS_RUNBOOK.md:38 attributes that statement to Gelato about Gelato's own quicknet beacon, it makes no claim about evmnet. Severity `critical` stands against the stated rubric ('randomness manipulable to select a chosen outcome'), but note that its proposed compensating control (a) 'make operator rotation actually possible' rests on finding #2, which I downgraded.

findings.title: No expiry or cancel path: a single unfulfilled request permanently welds FWA to its coordinator, blocks operator rotation forever and locks the coordinator's HYPE
findings.preconditions: One issued request that is never successfully fulfilled. Reachable by (a) a Gelato Gas Tank exhaustion or task/W3F outage spanning the request, (b) any persistent revert inside the consumer callback, or (c) deliberate withholding by the operator — free and instantaneous for the very party you need to be able to remove.
findings.scenario: `pendingRequestCount` is incremented at line 129 and decremented at exactly one place, line 158, inside a successful `fulfillRandomness`. There is no cancel, expire, admin-clear or timeout path anywhere in the contract. Ordering: (1) purchaser calls `FWA.acquire`, requestId=N, `pendingRequestCount=1`, `FWA.unfulfilledVrfCount=1`. (2) The operator never delivers. (3) After 30 blocks `processAcquisitions` expires the acquisition and refunds `priceEscrowed`; `unsettledAcquisitionCount` returns to 0 and depositors can withdraw — but `callbackObserved[N]` was never set, so `FWA.unfulfilledVrfCount` stays at 1 (FWA.sol:1492-1497). (4) The designed remedy `FWA.reconcileUnfulfilledVrfCount()` (FWA.sol:1463-1470) calls `s_vrfCoordinator.pendingRequestExists(vrfSubId)`, which returns `pendingRequestCount != 0` = true, so it reverts `VrfRequestsPending()` forever. (5) `FWA.setAddr(FWAConfigKeys.VRF_COORDINATOR, newCoordinator)` reverts `AcquisitionStateLocked()` forever (FWA.sol:2323-2325), and OPERATOR is `immutable` (line 41) so rotating the Gelato sender REQUIRES a new coordinator. (6) `FWA.configureVrfRequest` reverts forever (FWA.sol:1445-1449), freezing keyHash/callbackGasLimit. (7) `FWAVRFService._setCoverageConfig` can never lower the buffer (OutstandingCallbacks, FWAVRFService.sol:369-379), so `requiredSubscriptionBalance` stays inflated by `maxFulfillmentCostWei` (0.01 HYPE per .env.mainnet.example:29) and that much is permanently subtracted from `availableProcessorSurplus`. (8) `coordinator.withdrawNative` reverts `PendingRequests()` forever (line 208), permanently locking the whole `nativeSubscriptionBalance` — real HYPE routed there from purchaser fees by `FWAVRFService._ensureSubscriptionCoverage`. The test suite proves step (5) is reachable (test/FWADrandRelayIntegration.t.sol:81-87, `testMigrationIsRejectedWhileOldCoordinatorRequestIsInFlight`) but no test anywhere exercises a never-fulfilled request or `reconcileUnfulfilledVrfCount` — grep over test/ and script/ returns zero hits for that function.
findings.impact: Permanent, unrecoverable protocol lock-in to one randomness coordinator, plus permanent lock of the coordinator's native balance and of a slice of FWAVRFService surplus. Critically, this removes the ONLY on-chain remedy for the preceding finding: a malicious or compromised Gelato operator withholds fulfilment on one request at zero cost, after which it can never be replaced, and can then grind outcomes indefinitely. The only remaining response is `withdrawOnly` and a full wind-down plus redeployment of the entire FWA core. User NFTs remain withdrawable (verified: `unsettledAcquisitionCount` does return to 0 after expiry, so `withdrawListing` unlocks), so this is protocol destruction and native-fund lock rather than NFT theft.
findings.minimalFix: Add a terminal expiry to all three coordinators, e.g. `function expireRequest(uint256 requestId) external { Request storage r = requests[requestId]; if (r.status != RequestStatus.Pending) revert UnknownRequest(); if (block.number <= uint256(r.requestedAtBlock) + EXPIRY_BLOCKS) revert NotExpired(); r.status = RequestStatus.Expired; requestedHash[requestId] = bytes32(0); pendingRequestCount -= 1; emit RequestExpired(requestId); }` with `EXPIRY_BLOCKS` >= FWA's `selectionTimeoutBlocks` and no consumer callback (FWA already handles a never-arriving word via AcquisitionStatus.Expired, and `reconcileUnfulfilledVrfCount` exists precisely to absorb the accounting). Make it permissionless so no admin key is a liveness dependency. Also reject a late `fulfillRandomness` for an Expired request so the two paths cannot both fire.
findings.regressionTest: `testAbandonedRequestCanBeExpiredAndCoordinatorMigrated`: acquire once, never fulfil, `vm.roll` past EXPIRY_BLOCKS, call `expireRequest`, then assert in order — `coordinator.pendingRequestExists(1) == false`; `fwa.reconcileUnfulfilledVrfCount() == 1`; `fwa.setAddr(FWAConfigKeys.VRF_COORDINATOR, address(newCoordinator))` succeeds; `coordinator.withdrawNative(owner, balance)` succeeds. Add the mirror negative test asserting `expireRequest` reverts before the deadline and that a fulfilment after expiry reverts.

refutationNotes.reason: SURVIVES on mechanism but critical is materially overstated; correct severity is medium. Confirmed: pendingRequestCount is incremented at GelatoVRFCoordinator.sol:129 and decremented only at 158, with no cancel/expire/admin path, and the downstream locks are real (FWA.sol:1466 VrfRequestsPending, 2324 AcquisitionStateLocked on VRF_COORDINATOR, 1447 configureVrfRequest, FWAVRFService.sol:369-375 OutstandingCallbacks, coordinator line 208 PendingRequests). But two of the three stated preconditions do not produce the state, and the impact is far smaller than claimed. (1) A LATE fulfilment fully unsticks everything: FWA.fulfillRandomWords sets callbackObserved and decrements unfulfilledVrfCount at 1493-1497 BEFORE the deadline check, then returns without reverting for a non-Pending acquisition at 1499-1502, so the coordinator's `if (!success) revert ConsumerCallbackFailed()` passes and pendingRequestCount decrements. A Gas-Tank outage is therefore recoverable once refilled — drand rounds remain retrievable indefinitely. (2) A reverting consumer callback cannot persist the state either: the whole fulfillRandomness rolls back atomically and the request stays Pending (verified executably by testCallbackFailureRollsBackAndCanBeRetried, which I ran). Only a permanently hostile or permanently dead operator produces the terminal state. (3) 'Permanent, unrecoverable protocol lock-in… protocol destruction' is wrong: setBool(ACQUISITIONS_ENABLED) at FWA.sol:2295-2312 has NO acquisition-state lock, and setUint (2234) gates only on unsettledAcquisitionCount except for VRF_SUB_ID, so listing, acquiring, settling and withdrawing all keep working with unfulfilledVrfCount stuck at 1. What is genuinely and permanently lost is coordinator rotation/VRF_SUB_ID/configureVrfRequest/coverage reduction plus the coordinator's nativeSubscriptionBalance — which at the shipped .env values (FWA_MIN_RANDOMNESS_BUFFER_WEI = FWA_MAX_RANDOMNESS_COST_WEI = 1e16) is ~0.02 HYPE of protocol funds, not user funds or NFTs. Real, worth fixing (the proposed permissionless expireRequest is the right shape), but medium.

SURVIVES AS A DESIGN GAP, BUT 'critical / permanent / unrecoverable' IS NOT SUPPORTED. The mechanics check out: `pendingRequestCount` is incremented at GelatoVRFCoordinator.sol:129 and decremented only at 158; there is no cancel/expire/admin path in the file; FWA.sol:1466 reverts `VrfRequestsPending` while `pendingRequestExists`; FWA.sol:2324 reverts `AcquisitionStateLocked` for VRF_COORDINATOR while `unfulfilledVrfCount != 0`; OPERATOR is immutable (41); withdrawNative reverts `PendingRequests` (208); FWAVRFService.sol:372-375 reverts `OutstandingCallbacks`. Grep confirms no test or script exercises `reconcileUnfulfilledVrfCount`. But four things refute the irreversibility claim. (a) A LATE fulfilment always works and fully clears the state: the request stays `Pending`, so the operator can deliver at any time afterwards; FWA's callback then sets `callbackObserved`, decrements `unfulfilledVrfCount` (FWA.sol:1493-1497) and returns via the non-reverting `status != Pending` branch (1499-1502). The finding's own headline scenario (a) — Gas Tank exhaustion — is therefore fully recoverable by refilling and re-running the task. (b) ActivateHyperEVMMainnet.s.sol:68 requires `expectedOperator.code.length != 0`, i.e. the operator is a Gelato Automate dedicated-msg.sender proxy, which the project's own account can normally transact through — an off-chain manual clear path the finding never considers. (c) The 'same shape at DrandRelayCoordinator.sol' claim is wrong: the owner can `setRelayer(self, true)` (115) and deliver any 64-byte payload once `block.timestamp >= roundTimestamp(round)`, so a stuck 998 request is trivially clearable. (d) Scenario (b), 'any persistent revert inside the consumer callback', is asserted, not demonstrated — FWA's callback is deliberately non-reverting for unknown/duplicate/terminal/malformed fulfilments and the fast path is failure-isolated. Impact is also far smaller than stated: no user NFTs or ETH are at risk (the finding concedes this), and the only permanently stranded value is the coordinator's compatibility reserve, sized by .env.mainnet.example:28-29 at 0.02 HYPE, plus a one-time ratchet of `requiredSubscriptionBalance`. What genuinely remains: there is no on-chain terminal expiry, so a truly abandoned request (hostile operator, or Gelato dropping the task permanently) removes the coordinator-migration path with no on-chain remedy. That is a real hardening item worth fixing, not a critical.

findings.title: Safe activationBatch can open acquisitions before FWA.setRewards, permanently locking out the rewards module
findings.preconditions: Final owner is a Safe (the primary path per MAINNET_RELEASE_RUNBOOK_2026-07-26.md section 6 step 2). The Safe signers execute the generated release/mainnet-owner-actions.json. FWA.rewards() is still address(0) because preActivation was skipped, batched together with activationBatch, or executed second.
findings.scenario: PrepareMainnetOwnerActions.ps1 performs no RPC call at all: Get-Calldata only runs `cast calldata`, which is pure local ABI encoding. It therefore emits `preActivation` (FWA.setRewards) and `activationBatch` (Whitelist.setCollections + FWA.setBool(41,true)) unconditionally, at any point in the launch, with ordering enforced only by the `notes` strings on lines 79-85 and by prose in the runbook. Concrete ordering failure: (1) Safe executes activationBatch order 1 -> whitelist.setCollections([0xCollA], true); (2) Safe executes activationBatch order 2 -> fwa.setBool(41,true). FWA.setBool (FWA.sol:2295-2312) does NOT require rewards != address(0); it only calls r.startEmission() when rewards is already set. The product is now live with rewards unbound. (3) The first user calls listNFT -> activeListingCount becomes 1. (4) The Safe now executes preActivation. FWA.setRewards (FWA.sol:2347-2358) reverts InvalidConfig because of `if (activeListingCount != 0 || stagedCount != 0 || reservedStagedCount != 0) revert InvalidConfig()`. Note the asymmetry: the EOA path ActivateHyperEVMMainnet.s.sol:73 DOES enforce `address(fwa.rewards()) != address(rewards)` on-chain before opening acquisitions, so the stronger gate exists only on the secondary path while the documented primary (Safe) path has none.
findings.impact: setRewards is one-shot and additionally requires a completely empty pool, so on a public launch the window between whitelisting and the first deposit is seconds. Once missed, the $FWA emission leg of the protocol is permanently disabled: the 300,000,000 FWA transferred to FWARewardsHyperEVM by DeployNestModules.s.sol:96 can never be emitted, depositors and purchasers accrue nothing, and FWA.token() stays address(0) so acceptBidAsTokens is dead. Recovering the 300M requires FWARewardsHyperEVM.rescueTokens, which is gated on IFWARewardsCore(core).canRescueRewards() == withdrawOnly && unsettledAcquisitionCount == 0 (FWA.sol:2361-2363) - i.e. the owner must first put the whole product into withdraw-only mode.
findings.minimalFix: Give PrepareMainnetOwnerActions.ps1 a mandatory -RpcUrl and make emission conditional on live state: refuse to emit `activationBatch` unless `cast call $Fwa "rewards()(address)"` returns a non-zero address equal to -Rewards, and refuse to emit `preActivation` once `cast call $Fwa "collectionWhitelisted(address)(bool)"` is true for any -Collections entry or `activeListingCount()` is non-zero. Emit the two sections into separate files so they cannot be pasted into one Safe batch. Optionally deploy a tiny stateless guard contract whose `assertReadyToOpen(address fwa, address rewards)` is prepended (order 0) to activationBatch so the ordering is enforced on-chain rather than by a JSON note.
findings.regressionTest: Add a Solidity test FWAMainnetActivationOrdering.t.sol that deploys the core exactly as DeployHyperEVMMainnetCore does, then: (a) asserts fwa.setBool(ACQUISITIONS_ENABLED,true) followed by whitelist.setCollections + listNFT + fwa.setRewards reverts with InvalidConfig; (b) asserts the intended order (setRewards, then setCollections, then setBool) succeeds and rewards.emissionStart() != 0. Add a PowerShell case to TestReleaseScripts.ps1 asserting PrepareMainnetOwnerActions.ps1 throws when the on-chain rewards pointer is zero.

refutationNotes.reason: SURVIVES, severity overstated. Verified mechanism: PrepareMainnetOwnerActions.ps1 (C:/Users/eliot/Documents/FWA FORK/scripts/PrepareMainnetOwnerActions.ps1:21-52) only calls `cast calldata`, no RPC; FWA.sol:2295-2312 setBool(41,true) has no rewards!=0 requirement; FWA.sol:2347-2358 setRewards reverts InvalidConfig on activeListingCount/stagedCount/reservedStagedCount != 0; ActivateHyperEVMMainnet.s.sol:73 does enforce fwa.rewards()==rewards on the EOA path only. The asymmetry is real. THREE corrections. (1) The trigger is misidentified: the lock is caused by whitelist.setCollections alone, not by setBool(41). DeployHyperEVMMainnetCore.s.sol:92-99 leaves whitelistEnabled=true, withdrawOnly=false, acquisitionsEnabled=false, and FWA.sol:278-281 documents deposits working in the loading phase — so listNFT succeeds as soon as a collection is allowlisted, with acquisitions still closed. Order-2 setBool is irrelevant to the failure. (2) The 'batched together' variant is safe: $payload serialises preActivation before activationBatch (lines 76-77), so a Safe batch built in file order executes setRewards first. (3) Impact materially overstated: 'permanently disabled' and '300M can never be emitted' are both wrong. setRewards is blocked only while the pool is non-empty, so a withdraw-only drain restores it; and the 300M is recoverable via FWARewardsHyperEVM.sol:623 rescueTokens once the owner sets WITHDRAW_ONLY (FWA.sol:2361-2363), a maintenance window, not a write-off. The finding also omits three existing controls: BindNestRewards.s.sol:47-58 is the sanctioned setRewards path and asserts activeListingCount==0 and rewards==0 on-chain before broadcast; VerifyNestModules.s.sol:73 asserts address(fwa.rewards())==rewards, so the runbook section 6 step 1 attestation fails if rewards is unbound; and both the JSON `notes` and runbook 4.4 state the order. Net: an unenforced ordering hazard on the Safe path with a recoverable consequence and no user-fund exposure = medium, not high.

Mechanism partly real, impact false, severity two notches too high. VERIFIED: PrepareMainnetOwnerActions.ps1 makes no RPC call (Get-Calldata only shells `cast calldata`), FWA.setBool (vendor/fwa-reference-union/src/FWA.sol:2295-2312) has no rewards!=0 precondition, and ActivateHyperEVMMainnet.s.sol:73 does carry the stronger on-chain check that the Safe artefact lacks. REFUTED on two grounds. (1) 'Permanently disabled' is wrong. setRewards' blockers (FWA.sol:2349-2350) are transient, not terminal: withdrawListing (FWA.sol:1056-1083) has NO time lock and only requires unsettledAcquisitionCount==0, and setBool(WITHDRAW_ONLY,true) blocks new deposits (line 808) and new acquisitions (line 1356) so activeListingCount can only fall. Once it reaches 0 the owner calls setRewards, which — because acquisitionsEnabled is already true — immediately fires r.startEmission() (line 2356) and fully recovers. In the finding's own timeline exactly one listing exists, so recovery is minutes; no user ETH or NFT is at risk and the 300M FWA never leaves FWARewardsHyperEVM. rescueTokens/withdraw-only is therefore not the remedy the finding claims it is. (2) 'Ordering enforced only by notes/prose' is wrong: NEST_DEPLOYMENT_RUNBOOK.md section 7 and MAINNET_RELEASE_RUNBOOK section 4.4 both interpose VerifyNestModules.s.sol, and that script reverts InvalidWiring at lines 73-74 precisely when address(fwa.rewards())!=rewards or fwa.token()!=token. NEST_E2E_CONFIRMED (demanded by ActivateHyperEVMMainnet.s.sol:47) is only set after it passes. A machine-checkable gate exists in the documented flow. What survives is a low-severity asymmetry worth closing: the Safe JSON carries no state attestation of its own.

findings.title: Nest-side contract ownership is never attested, and FWA_OWNER is read with a deployer-defaulting envOr, so the deployer EOA can retain the token, rewards, adapter and LP-fee admin
findings.preconditions: FWA_OWNER is absent from the environment of the shell that runs DeployNestToken.s.sol and/or DeployNestModules.s.sol (for example the operator ran ImportEnvFile.ps1 in a different window, or Foundry's automatic project-root .env supplied only some names), or the ownership transfer transaction is dropped/reverted while the rest of the launch proceeds.
findings.scenario: Both Nest deploy scripts resolve the final owner with `address finalOwner = vm.envOr("FWA_OWNER", deployer);` (DeployNestToken.s.sol:56, DeployNestModules.s.sol:63) instead of the strict `vm.envAddress` used by DeployHyperEVMMainnetCore.s.sol:60. When FWA_OWNER is unset, finalOwner silently becomes the temporary deployer EOA. Every subsequent guard still passes: DeployNestModules.s.sol:71 only checks finalOwner != address(0); lines 103-107 skip the transferOwnership block entirely because finalOwner == deployer; DeployNestToken.s.sol:78 constructs FWANestLiquidityLocker with owner_ = deployer. Nothing downstream catches it. VerifyNestModules.s.sol:55-78 checks 25 wiring equalities but never reads token.owner(), rewards.owner(), adapter.owner() or locker.owner(). ActivateHyperEVMMainnet.s.sol:63-76 checks splitter.owner() == fwa.owner() but never the four Nest owners. Contrast VerifyHyperEVMCore.s.sol:61-72, which correctly asserts coordinator.owner(), service.owner(), whitelist.owner() and splitter.owner() all equal fwa.owner(). Result: the launch completes, every attestation script prints green, and the audit trail shows a fully wired mainnet system whose Nest half is owned by a hot deployer key.
findings.impact: Unauthorised residual admin power over user-facing value and the trading switch: FWATokenNest.setExternalBuysEnabled (FWATokenNest.sol:171) lets the deployer open or close public $FWA trading unilaterally, bypassing the Safe-only manualTradingControls the runbook section 7 promises; setDistributor (line 159) grants any address a permanent exemption from the transfer restrictions in _afterTokenTransfer; setBuybackSqrtPriceLimitX96 (line 240) and setRouteSplit (line 232) let the deployer make every protocol buyback executable at an arbitrary price, which is directly extractable by sandwiching buyback(); FWARewardsHyperEVM.sweepEmptyEpoch and setForcedTokenShareBps (lines 602-619) redirect emissions; FWANestSwapAdapter.recoverForcedHype (line 139) sweeps native HYPE held by the adapter; and FWANestLiquidityLocker.setFeeRecipient (FWANestLiquidityLocker.sol:54-58) permanently redirects every trading fee accrued by the locked 500M-FWA LP position, which is the only recoverable value in a position that is by design never withdrawable.
findings.minimalFix: Replace `vm.envOr("FWA_OWNER", deployer)` with `vm.envAddress("FWA_OWNER")` in DeployNestToken.s.sol:56 and DeployNestModules.s.sol:63 so an unset variable fails closed. Add a post-broadcast assertion block to DeployNestModules.s.sol mirroring ResumeHyperEVMCore.s.sol:99-104. refutationNotes.reason: SURVIVES, severity overstated. Every structural claim verified: DeployNestToken.s.sol:56 and DeployNestModules.s.sol:63 use vm.envOr("FWA_OWNER", deployer) while DeployHyperEVMMainnetCore.s.sol:60 uses strict vm.envAddress; DeployNestModules.s.sol:71 checks only finalOwner!=0 and 103-107 skips transferOwnership when finalOwner==deployer; VerifyNestModules.s.sol:55-78 contains 25+ wiring equalities and reads fwa.owner() at line 75 for the splitter but never token/rewards/adapter/locker owner; ActivateHyperEVMMainnet.s.sol:63-76 likewise checks only splitter.owner(); VerifyHyperEVMCore.s.sol:57-72 does assert coordinator/service/whitelist/splitter owners == fwa.owner(). The owner powers cited are all real and onlyOwner (FWATokenNest.sol:159,171,232,240; FWARewardsHyperEVM.sol:602,608; FWANestSwapAdapter.sol:139; FWANestLiquidityLocker.sol:54). One partial catch the finding missed: ActivateNestMarket.s.sol:54 requires vm.addr(OWNER_PRIVATE_KEY)==token.owner(), so on the EOA path opening public trading fails closed if the token is still deployer-owned. One point that sharpens it: the identical envOr in DeploySplitterHyperEVM.s.sol:50 IS caught downstream by DeployHyperEVMMainnetCore.s.sol:66-68 (splitter.owner()!=finalOwner reverts), proving the pattern is normally backstopped and the Nest half is the sole unbackstopped case. Severity: with .env.mainnet.example:5 shipping FWA_OWNER=0x0 (which reverts InvalidAddress at line 71) the realistic failure is a stale-but-controlled address rather than a hot deployer key, and the state is fully recoverable by re-calling transferOwnership while the deployer key is held. This is the rubric's 'gate that fails open under a plausible operational error' = medium, not the unauthorised-admin-power-by-design that high describes.

The stated precondition is unreachable in the audited tree. (a) .env.mainnet.example:5 ships FWA_OWNER=0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000 — an unfilled template does NOT fall through to the deployer; envOr returns address(0) and both scripts revert InvalidAddress (DeployNestToken.s.sol:67, DeployNestModules.s.sol:71). Fail-closed. (b) The 'different window' path is refuted empirically. The project-root .env in the audited tree defines FWA_OWNER (42-char address), and I proved Foundry's dotenv never overrides process env: running `FWA_TOKENOMICS_CONFIRMED=false ./.tools/foundry/forge.exe script script/DeployNestModules.s.sol:DeployNestModules` reverted TokenomicsNotConfirmed even though .env sets that key to true. Precedence is shell > .env, so .env fills FWA_OWNER whenever the shell does not and envOr never reaches its deployer default. Note this makes finding #2 and finding #3 mutually exclusive: #3's whole mechanism is that the auto-loaded .env supplies missing values. (c) A genuinely unimported shell also loses PRIVATE_KEY, FWA_ADDRESS and NEST_MAINNET_DEPLOYMENT_CONFIRMED (=false in .env) — the run fails loudly, not silently. (d) A deployer-owned splitter is separately caught: DeployHyperEVMMainnetCore.s.sol:64-67 reverts InvalidSplitter unless splitter.owner()==FWA_OWNER. ACCURATE AND SURVIVING AS LOW: VerifyNestModules.s.sol:55-78 and ActivateHyperEVMMainnet.s.sol:65-76 genuinely never read token/rewards/adapter/locker owner(), unlike VerifyHyperEVMCore.s.sol:61-72 which attests all four core owners — a real attestation-coverage gap. All cited admin functions exist as described (FWATokenNest.sol:159/171/232/240, FWARewardsHyperEVM.sol:602/608, FWANestSwapAdapter.sol:139, FWANestLiquidityLocker.sol:54-58). But 'unauthorised admin power' is the wrong frame: this is failure to relinquish, contingent on an operator error that the code already blocks.

findings.title: Pool price initialization and the permanent LP lock are one-shot irreversible mainnet actions with no dedicated confirmation gate, driven by env vars whose defaults are wrong and are already present in the auto-loaded testnet .env
findings.preconditions: Mainnet launch has reached Nest phase D/F. NEST_MAINNET_DEPLOYMENT_CONFIRMED is already true, which the launch requires from its very first broadcast. FWA_INITIAL_SQRT_PRICE_X96 and/or FWA_LP_RANGE_WIDTH_TICKS come from a template default or from the project-root .env that Foundry loads automatically for every forge script invocation.
findings.scenario: NEST_MAINNET_DEPLOYMENT_CONFIRMED is not a per-phase gate: DeploySplitterHyperEVM.s.sol:44-46 already demands it for the very first mainnet broadcast (runbook section 4.1), so it is true for the entire remainder of the launch. InitializeNestMarket.s.sol and LaunchNestMarket.s.sol have no other flag whatsoever (lines 27-29 and 38-40 respectively) - unlike DeployNestToken (FWA_TOKENOMICS_CONFIRMED), ConfigureNestPool (NEST_ADMIN_ACTIONS_CONFIRMED) or BindNestRewards (NEST_CORE_BINDING_CONFIRMED). Their critical numeric inputs are read raw: `vm.envUint("FWA_INITIAL_SQRT_PRICE_X96")` (InitializeNestMarket.s.sol:35) and `vm.envInt("FWA_LP_RANGE_WIDTH_TICKS")` (LaunchNestMarket.s.sol:46). .env.mainnet.example:61 ships FWA_INITIAL_SQRT_PRICE_X96=79228162514264337593543950336, which is exactly 2^96, i.e. a 1:1 $FWA/wHYPE price, and the project-root .env currently on disk contains that identical value plus FWA_LP_RANGE_WIDTH_TICKS=3600. Concrete failure: the operator runs `forge script script/InitializeNestMarket.s.sol --rpc-url hyperevm_mainnet --broadcast` in a shell where .env.mainnet.local was never imported. Foundry's dotenv supplies the 1:1 price. FWATokenNest.initializeMarket (FWATokenNest.sol:253-286) accepts it (the only range check is MIN_SQRT_RATIO < p < MAX_SQRT_RATIO), sets marketInitialized = true and reverts MarketAlreadyInitialized on any retry. LaunchNestMarket then mints the single-sided position at that price and calls FWANestLiquidityLocker.bind, which is one-shot (FWANestLiquidityLocker.sol:45-52), inside finalizeLaunch which sets launched = true permanently.
findings.impact: Permanent, unrecoverable misplacement of 500,000,000 $FWA - 50% of total supply. FWANestLiquidityLocker is documented and implemented with no NFT transfer and no decreaseLiquidity path (FWANestLiquidityLocker.sol:10-11), FWATokenNest.finalizeLaunch reverts AlreadyLaunched, initializeMarket reverts MarketAlreadyInitialized, and the Algebra factory keeps one pool per (wHYPE, FWA) pair, so the only remedy is redeploying the token and abandoning the launched one. At a 1:1 initial price the entire LP is immediately arbitraged out of the protocol's intended range. Same class of exposure for a stale FWA_LEGACY_ALLOCATION_RECIPIENT, which routes 200,000,000 $FWA (DeployNestModules.s.sol:99) and whose current .env value is a single test EOA.
findings.minimalFix: (1) Add dedicated one-use gates: require NEST_MARKET_PRICE_CONFIRMED in InitializeNestMarket.s.sol and NEST_LP_LOCK_CONFIRMED in LaunchNestMarket.s.sol, both listed in .env.mainnet.example defaulting to false. (2) Make both scripts hard-require `block.chainid == 998 || block.chainid == 999` (they currently have no positive chain allowlist). (3) Remove the numeric default from .env.mainnet.example:61 (leave it empty so vm.envUint fails closed) or require a second variable FWA_INITIAL_SQRT_PRICE_X96_ECHO that must match. (4) Namespace mainnet variables (MAINNET_FWA_INITIAL_SQRT_PRICE_X96, ...) so Foundry's auto-loaded testnet .env can never satisfy a mainnet script, or have ImportEnvFile.ps1 refuse to run while a project-root .env exists.
findings.regressionTest: Add a script self-test that invokes InitializeNestMarket and LaunchNestMarket with the new flags unset and asserts they revert. Add a Solidity test asserting FWATokenNest.initializeMarket reverts MarketAlreadyInitialized on a second call and that finalizeLaunch reverts AlreadyLaunched, plus a test that FWANestLiquidityLocker exposes no path that moves the bound tokenId. Add a TestReleaseCandidate.ps1 preflight step that fails if a project-root .env exists while targeting chain 999.

refutationNotes.reason: PARTIALLY REFUTED — core hardening point survives, but the concrete scenario and the impact mechanism are both wrong; severity overstated. (a) The stated scenario is impossible. I tested forge's dotenv precedence empirically: with FWA_TOKENOMICS_CONFIRMED forced to "false" in the process env, DeployNestModules reverted TokenomicsNotConfirmed; with it unset, the project .env's `true` was used and execution continued to InvalidContract. So .env only BACKFILLS absent variables. The root .env (line 78) sets NEST_MAINNET_DEPLOYMENT_CONFIRMED=false, therefore a shell where '.env.mainnet.local was never imported' reverts MainnetNotConfirmed at InitializeNestMarket.s.sol:27 and never broadcasts. The only live path is an imported mainnet file that omits FWA_INITIAL_SQRT_PRICE_X96 — or, far more simply, one that leaves the template value untouched, which needs no .env at all. (b) The impact is backwards. sqrtPriceX96=2^96 is 1 FWA = 1 wHYPE, i.e. ~40bn FDV on a 1e9 supply — absurdly HIGH. LaunchNestMarket.s.sol:61-67 and FWATokenNest.sol:310-316 place the single-sided position strictly above spot, so at 1:1 nothing is 'immediately arbitraged out of the protocol's intended range'; the LP is simply unbuyable and the market is stillborn. The failure is a dead market, not extraction. (c) The FWA_LEGACY_ALLOCATION_RECIPIENT limb is refuted: .env.mainnet.example:60 ships 0x0, vm.envAddress returns zero and DeployNestModules.s.sol:71 reverts InvalidAddress — it fails closed on the template. What survives and is worth fixing: FWATokenNest.sol:261 bounds the price only by MIN/MAX_SQRT_RATIO; initializeMarket (255) and finalizeLaunch (295) are one-shot; FWANestLiquidityLocker has no transfer or decreaseLiquidity path (verified, file is 75 lines); and .env.mainnet.example:61 ships a concrete plausible-looking numeric default for an irreversible one-shot value with no second-source echo. That is a real launch-configuration hazard = medium. No user funds or NFTs are exposed and the 500M LP was designed to be permanently locked regardless, so high is not supportable.

The concrete failure path is self-contradictory and the impact is directionally wrong. (1) The trigger is 'a shell where .env.mainnet.local was never imported, so Foundry's dotenv supplies the 1:1 price' — but the same auto-loaded .env sets NEST_MAINNET_DEPLOYMENT_CONFIRMED=false (I read the file), and I verified empirically that shell values win over .env and never the reverse (see my verdict on finding #2). In that shell InitializeNestMarket.s.sol:27-29 reverts MainnetNotConfirmed. Fail-closed. To have the flag true the operator must have run ImportEnvFile.ps1 on .env.mainnet.local, and that script imports every key in the file (scripts/ImportEnvFile.ps1:7-18); since the file is copied from .env.mainnet.example it carries its own FWA_INITIAL_SQRT_PRICE_X96 (line 61) and FWA_LP_RANGE_WIDTH_TICKS (62). The testnet .env can therefore never be the source of a mainnet price. Same refutation applies verbatim to the FWA_LEGACY_ALLOCATION_RECIPIENT variant. (2) The impact is wrong: 2^96 is 1 FWA = 1 wHYPE, an absurdly HIGH launch price. finalizeLaunch (FWATokenNest.sol:311-317) forces the single-sided FWA position to sit at or above spot, so it only sells FWA as FWA gets dearer — a too-high start produces a dead market nobody buys into, not an LP 'immediately arbitraged out of the protocol's intended range'. No attacker extracts the 500M. CORRECT AND SURVIVING AS LOW: the one-shot claims hold (initializeMarket MarketAlreadyInitialized at FWATokenNest.sol:255, finalizeLaunch AlreadyLaunched at 289, locker bind AlreadyBound at FWANestLiquidityLocker.sol:47, no transfer/decreaseLiquidity path), and .env.mainnet.example:61-62 is the only place in that template shipping semantically meaningful defaults where every other sensitive value is zeroed/false/empty. Worth fixing as hardening; not high.

findings.lens: Indexer (Goldsky subgraph) correctness and its consumption b
findings.title: FWA data source calls ERC721.tokenURI without declaring the ERC721 ABI — every deposit event halts the subgraph
findings.preconditions: Subgraph deployed from the rendered manifest (indexer/subgraph.yaml, byte-identical structure in indexer/build/subgraph.yaml). Any `ListingStaged` or `NFTListed` event is emitted, i.e. the first deposit ever made.
findings.scenario: `src/mapping.ts` runs inside the `FWA` data source. `captureTokenURI()` (mapping.ts:89-93) executes `ERC721.bind(Address.fromBytes(listing.collection)).try_tokenURI(...)`. The generated binding is `new ERC721("ERC721", address)` (indexer/generated/ERC721_0/ERC721.ts:39-41), and graph-ts forwards that literal contract name to the host: `SmartContractCall(this._name, ...)` (indexer/node_modules/@graphprotocol/graph-ts/chain/ethereum.ts:671-682). graph-node resolves the name against the *calling data source's* `abis` list. The `FWA` data source declares only `- name: FWA` (subgraph.template.yaml:23-25; confirmed in the rendered indexer/subgraph.yaml:23-25 and indexer/build/subgraph.yaml:23-25). `ERC721` is declared only on the separate `ERC721_0` data source (subgraph.yaml:92-94). Concrete sequence: deploy, depositor calls `listNFT(collection, tokenId)` with a quiet pool, FWA emits `NFTListed`, `handleNFTListed` reaches line 156 `captureTokenURI(listing)`, the host export returns a `HostExportError` ("Could not find ABI for contract \"ERC721\", try adding it to the 'abis' section of the subgraph manifest"). `try_` only converts an EVM revert to null — it does not catch a host error — so the handler traps. The subgraph stops advancing at that block and never indexes anything after the first deposit. `graph codegen`/`graph build` do not catch this: the AssemblyScript import `../generated/ERC721_0/ERC721` (mapping.ts:29) resolves because a collection data source exists, and graph-cli performs no cross-data-source ABI-usage validation.
findings.impact: Total, permanent loss of the indexer from the first deposit onward. Because the frontend routes `getUserPositions`, `acquisitionTickets`, `getActivity`, `getIndexedOwnedEligibleNFTs` and the pool grid through the indexer whenever `NEXT_PUBLIC_INDEXER_URL` is set, the product ships with an empty Positions screen, no reveal, no owned-NFT list in the deposit flow and an empty activity tape — while the EnvBanner shows nothing (see the `indexer.status === "down"` finding). Downstream that is the mechanism by which purchasers miss the 24 h settlement window. Secondary consequence of the same coupling: if the mainnet manifest ever ships with zero collections, `render-manifest.mjs` deletes `src/generated-collections/` and emits no `ERC721_0` data source, so `graph codegen` never produces `generated/ERC721_0/ERC721` and the `src/mapping.ts` import breaks the build. Residual-risk note: in the unlikely case graph-node degraded the missing ABI to a null return instead of a trap, the consequence downgrades to `Listing.tokenURI` being permanently null (no NFT names/images from the index) — still a defect, and the fix is identical.
findings.minimalFix:
Add the ERC721 ABI to the FWA data source in `indexer/subgraph.template.yaml` so the binding resolves in the calling context:
```yaml
      abis:
        - name: FWA
          file: ./abis/FWA.json
        - name: ERC721
          file: ./abis/ERC721.json
```
Also decouple `src/mapping.ts` from the generated per-collection module: import `ERC721` from a stable `generated/FWA/...`-style path (or declare a dedicated non-indexed ABI-only entry) instead of `../generated/ERC721_0/ERC721`, so a zero-collection manifest still builds.
findings.regressionTest: Add a Matchstick test (`indexer/tests/`) that runs `handleNFTListed` against a mocked `tokenURI(uint256)` via `createMockedFunction(collection, "tokenURI", "tokenURI(uint256):(string)")` and asserts `Listing["1"].tokenURI == "ipfs://…"`. Matchstick resolves contract calls through the manifest ABIs, so the test fails today and passes after the ABI is added. Complement with a CI assertion over the rendered `subgraph.yaml`: for every `ethereum.SmartContract` name referenced by a data source's mapping file, that name must appear in the same data source's `abis` list.

refutationNotes.reason: Mechanism verified end to end. subgraph.template.yaml:23-25, the rendered indexer/subgraph.yaml:23-25 and indexer/build/subgraph.yaml all declare only `- name: FWA` on the FWA data source; indexer/generated/ERC721_0/ERC721.ts:39-41 is `new ERC721("ERC721", address)` and graph-ts forwards that literal name (node_modules/@graphprotocol/graph-ts/chain/ethereum.ts SmartContract.tryCall -> `new SmartContractCall(this._name, ...)`), which graph-node resolves against the CALLING data source's abis list. captureTokenURI runs unconditionally at mapping.ts:127 and :156, and try_ only converts an EVM revert, not a host error. `graph build` does not catch it (the build/ output exists and is clean). So the defect is real. Severity is overstated at high: nothing here locks funds or NFTs, the chain stays the source of truth, and a subgraph is redeployable, so no consequence is permanent or irreversible — the high bucket in this rubric requires that. The impact narrative is also self-inconsistent: if the handler traps on the FIRST deposit, no listing is ever discoverable, so no acquisition and no 24h settlement window can ever exist to be missed. It also fails loudly, not silently — a stalled (non-deterministic-retry) subgraph reports hasIndexingErrors=false with a growing lag, so getConnectionHealth returns "lagging" (ViemProtocolClient.ts:695) and EnvBanner renders the amber "Indexer N blocks behind" bar, on top of a visibly empty pool grid from block zero. Launch-blocking product defect, medium.

Code facts all check out. indexer/subgraph.template.yaml:23-25, the rendered indexer/subgraph.yaml:23-25 and indexer/build/subgraph.yaml:23-25 declare only `- name: FWA` on the FWA data source; ERC721 is declared solely on ERC721_0 (subgraph.yaml:92-94, build:96-98). indexer/generated/ERC721_0/ERC721.ts:39-41 is `new ERC721("ERC721", address)` and graph-ts forwards that literal name into SmartContractCall (node_modules/@graphprotocol/graph-ts/chain/ethereum.ts:671-698), which graph-node resolves against the *calling* data source's `mapping.abis`. captureTokenURI is reached on the first deposit from both mapping.ts:127 (handleListingStaged) and mapping.ts:156 (handleNFTListed), and `try_` only converts an EVM revert, not a host error. No deployed subgraph refutes it empirically: frontend/INTEGRATION_NEEDS.md:25 still lists the Goldsky endpoint as a missing external input, so this has never run against a live chain. The zero-collection build-break corollary is also real (render-manifest.mjs:25-27 rm's src/generated-collections and only emits ERC721_x inside the collections loop at line 29, so codegen never produces generated/ERC721_0 and the mapping.ts:29 import fails). Severity is overstated, though. `high` in this rubric means fund/NFT lock-up, insolvency, permanent DoS of settlement/withdrawals or an irreversible early open — none apply: settlement, withdrawals and every write guard stay on-chain, the frontend re-reads FWA.listings before signing, and a subgraph redeploy fixes it with no contract change and no user exposure. The failure is also the loudest possible one: it triggers on the very first ListingStaged/NFTListed ever emitted, so the pool grid, activity tape and positions are all empty at once, and TopBar.tsx:32 renders a persistent red "Indexer down" chip. The stated downstream chain (users silently miss a 24 h settlement window) requires the indexer to work for a while and then fail quietly; this one cannot reach that state because nothing is ever indexed. Real must-fix launch blocker for the indexer, but medium.

findings.lens: Indexer (Goldsky subgraph) correctness and its consumption b
findings.title: Time-critical settlement state (allocated listings, acquisition tickets, reveal) is indexer-only with no on-chain fallback
findings.preconditions: `NEXT_PUBLIC_INDEXER_URL` is set (the documented mainnet configuration). The subgraph is stalled, failed, partially reorged, behind, or returns an incomplete result set — for example because of the missing-ERC721-ABI finding above.
findings.scenario: `getUserPositions` derives `deposited`, `allocated`, `depositedAllocated`, `settled`, `stuck` and `claimable.listingFees` exclusively from `getIndexedListingsForAccount(account)` (line 864), and `pendingAcquisitions` exclusively from `indexedAcquisitionTickets(account)` (line 754). Both take the indexer branch unconditionally when `indexerUrl` is truthy; the on-chain enumeration paths that exist (`getAllListingsDirect`, ViemProtocolClient.ts:525-537, and the `lastIssuedSequence`/`requestIdAtSequence` walk, 755-805) are dead in that configuration and there is no cross-check, no empty-result fallback and no `hasIndexingErrors` gate. Concrete sequence: purchaser calls `acquire`, the coordinator delivers the word, `processAcquisitions` emits `NFTAllocated(requestId, listingId=42, purchaser, …)` at T0. The subgraph has stalled at a block before T0, so the query returns `{ acquisitions: [] }` and `{ listings: [] }` with HTTP 200 and no GraphQL error. `usePositions()` resolves successfully with empty arrays, `useRevealQueue` never queues a reveal (useRevealQueue.ts:94 requires `t.phase === "allocated"`), and the Positions screen shows zero allocated positions. At T0 + `settlementWindow` (24 h) the depositor calls `depositorReclaimNFT(42)` (FWA.sol:1817-1824); the NFT returns to the depositor and the purchaser receives only `settlementDiscountBps` of the backing.
findings.impact: A purchaser who paid the full acquisition price loses the NFT and is paid only the discounted backing, purely because of an off-chain data failure — no contract bug, no attacker required. The same omission hides `stuck` recoveries and `claimable.listingFees`. Note that a *hard* indexer outage is comparatively safe (indexerQuery throws `INDEXER_DOWN` and the query errors visibly, ViemProtocolClient.ts:174-180); the dangerous mode is exactly the silent one — stalled, pruned or partially indexed — where empty is indistinguishable from "you have nothing". This also contradicts INTEGRATION_NEEDS.md:33 ("aucun droit ni quote n'en dépend") and indexer/README.md:42-46, which describe the subgraph as discovery-only: rights and quotes indeed do not depend on it, but the user's awareness of a 24-hour deadline does.
findings.minimalFix: Make the settlement-critical slice fail closed and self-heal: (1) in `getUserPositions`/`acquisitionTickets`, always read `_meta { block { number } hasIndexingErrors }` alongside the data and throw `INDEXER_DOWN` when `hasIndexingErrors` is true or when the lag exceeds a hard threshold, so the screen shows an error rather than an empty portfolio; (2) always cross-check the ticket set against the chain by walking `lastIssuedSequence`/`requestIdAtSequence` for the connected account (the code already exists at lines 755-805) and unioning it with the indexed set — this is bounded by the account's own request count, not by pool size; (3) render an explicit banner on PositionsScreen when the indexed head is behind the RPC head, rather than an empty tab.
findings.regressionTest: Vitest, alongside the existing cases in `frontend/src/protocol/viem/ViemProtocolClient.test.ts`: stub `fetch` to return `{ listings: [], acquisitions: [] }` while stubbing the on-chain reads so `lastIssuedSequence = 1` and `acquisitions(requestId)` reports status `Fulfilled` with `listingId = 42`; assert `getUserPositions(account).allocated` contains listing 42 (or that the call rejects with `INDEXER_DOWN`) — it must never resolve to an empty `allocated` array while the chain says otherwise. Add a second case with `_meta.hasIndexingErrors === true` asserting the call rejects.

refutationNotes.reason: The wiring is as described: with indexerUrl set, acquisitionTickets short-circuits to the indexed path (line 753-754) and getUserPositions derives every bucket from getIndexedListingsForAccount (line 864); hydrateIndexedListing revalidates each returned row on-chain but a row absent from the index is simply absent, and no call gates on _meta/hasIndexingErrors. Worth fixing — but high is wrong on three counts. (1) There is no protocol defect and no total loss: depositorReclaimNFT pays the purchaser settlementDiscountBps of the backing (FWA.sol:1813-1825) and finalizeUnsettled guarantees neither asset locks (FWA.sol:1828-1838); this is a designed timeout outcome, reached by user inaction, fully visible on the explorer. (2) The 'silent' premise mostly collapses into the EnvBanner finding: a merely stalled subgraph yields hasIndexingErrors=false and lag>20, i.e. status "lagging" and a visible amber banner; only the hasIndexingErrors=true case is silent, and a hard outage throws INDEXER_DOWN visibly (lines 174-180). (3) The recommended remedy is materially wrong: lastIssuedSequence is a GLOBAL counter (FWA.sol:275, incremented at 1371), and the walk at ViemProtocolClient.ts:755-805 iterates every protocol-wide sequence with three RPC calls each and only filters by account afterwards at line 768 — it is bounded by total protocol acquisitions, not 'the account's own request count', so adopting it as an always-on cross-check would be an RPC-cost failure at mainnet scale. Correct severity: medium (a UI that fails open under a plausible operational failure).

The code facts are right: getIndexedListingsForAccount (ViemProtocolClient.ts:551) and acquisitionTickets (753-754) both take the indexed branch whenever indexerUrl is truthy, the on-chain lastIssuedSequence/requestIdAtSequence walk (755-805) is dead in that configuration, getAllListingsDirect (525-537) is only reached when indexerUrl is empty, and there is no hasIndexingErrors gate or empty-result cross-check inside getUserPositions. What does not survive is the premise that carries the `high` severity — that the failure is silent and indistinguishable from "you have nothing". TopBar.tsx:28-36 is rendered on every route by AppShell.tsx:22 and maps getConnectionHealth directly to a persistent status capsule: `indexer.status === "down"` renders a red dot labelled "Indexer down", `"lagging"` renders an amber "−N blocks". getConnectionHealth (ViemProtocolClient.ts:684-702) sets "down" on hasIndexingErrors AND on any query failure, and "lagging" at lag > 20 blocks. So a stalled subgraph (lag grows past 20 within seconds on HyperEVM) and an errored subgraph are both surfaced continuously, on the Positions screen included. A hard outage additionally throws INDEXER_DOWN visibly (174-180). What remains is the genuinely hypothetical mode: a subgraph reporting a healthy _meta at the chain head while returning incomplete rows — not a documented graph-node failure mode, no attacker, no protocol defect, and fully recoverable by unsetting NEXT_PUBLIC_INDEXER_URL to fall back to the direct reader that already exists. Unioning the on-chain ticket walk with the indexed set is worthwhile defence in depth, hence low, not high.

findings.lens: FWA core, parity and liability conservation (HyperEVM mainne
findings.title: Mainnet deploys with Ethereum's 30-block selection timeout, a value already proven wrong on HyperEVM
findings.preconditions: Chain 999. `DeployHyperEVMMainnetCore` is run, then `ActivateHyperEVMMainnet` (or the Safe `activationBatch`). No script, verifier or Safe calldata anywhere in the release path calls `setUint(FWAConfigKeys.SELECTION_TIMEOUT_BLOCKS, ...)` (verified by grep across the whole tree: the only writer is `script/RetryTimedOutDrandGameplayE2E.s.sol:60`, which is hard-gated to chain 998).
findings.scenario: FWA.sol:264 initialises `selectionTimeoutBlocks = 30`, sized for Ethereum's 12s blocks (~6 minutes). `FWA_PARITY_MANIFEST.md:37` records HyperEVM as ~1s fast blocks, and §6 line 149 explicitly states the value must become 360 on HyperEVM 'pour conserver environ six minutes'. `TESTNET_998_DEPLOYMENTS.md:145-156` documents that on 998 the first live request was classified `TimedOut` precisely because of the 30-block window, and that the value was raised to 360 in tx 0x6bfa0ee0…. The mainnet path never carries that lesson forward. Concretely: purchaser calls `acquire{value: fee + vrfFee}`; `_openAcquisition` (FWA.sol:1373) snapshots `wordDeadlineBlock = block.number + 30` ≈ 30 seconds of wall clock. Gelato's operator must observe `RequestedRandomness`, wait for drand round `currentRound+1` to publish (1-3s), run its web3 function and land a ~1M-gas fulfilment tx. Any latency past ~30 blocks makes `fulfillRandomWords` take the `block.number > meta.wordDeadlineBlock` branch (FWA.sol:1505-1510) → `TimedOut` → `processAcquisitions` credits an `Expired` pull refund of `priceEscrowed` only.
findings.impact: Systematic failure of the core product function at launch. The refund covers only the pool fee: the separately forwarded VRF service fee (`vrfService.prepareRequests{value: vrf}`, FWA.sol:1284) is already spent and is never refunded on any expiry path, so every purchaser loses the full randomness fee for nothing. Worse, the owner cannot repair it under load: `setUint` reverts with `AcquisitionStateLocked` whenever `unsettledAcquisitionCount != 0` (FWA.sol:2235), so the fix requires first draining every in-flight (expiring) sequence.
findings.minimalFix: Add `fwa.setUint(FWAConfigKeys.SELECTION_TIMEOUT_BLOCKS, <value>)` to `DeployHyperEVMMainnetCore.run()` immediately after the `TOP_LISTING_SHARE_BPS` line, sourced from a mandatory env var (e.g. `FWA_SELECTION_TIMEOUT_BLOCKS`, defaulted to 360 as on 998 and validated against `requestConfirmations + MIN_CALLBACK_SLACK_BLOCKS`), and add `fwa.selectionTimeoutBlocks() != expected` to the `InvalidWiring` predicate in both `ActivateHyperEVMMainnet.s.sol` and `VerifyHyperEVMCore.s.sol` so activation is impossible with the Ethereum default.
findings.regressionTest: Foundry test `testMainnetTimeoutIsNotTheEthereumDefault`: deploy the core through the mainnet script path with `vm.chainId(999)` and assert `pool.selectionTimeoutBlocks() >= 360`; plus a lifecycle test that rolls exactly `selectionTimeoutBlocks` blocks between `acquire` and the coordinator callback and asserts the acquisition reaches `Fulfilled`, not `Expired`.

Neither ActivateHyperEVMMainnet.s.sol:65-76 nor VerifyHyperEVMCore.s.sol:61-72 asserts it. FWA_PARITY_MANIFEST.md line 149 is the project's own statement that '30 blocs Ethereum deviennent 360 blocs HyperEVM pour conserver environ six minutes', and TESTNET_998_DEPLOYMENTS.md:145-156 records the live TimedOut and the raise to 360. The VRF fee is genuinely non-refundable: _creditAcquisitionRefund (FWA.sol:1584-1592) returns only priceEscrowed, while the vrf leg left at FWA.sol:1284. SEVERITY OVERSTATED. (1) 'The owner cannot repair it under load' is wrong: setBool (FWA.sol:2295) carries NO AcquisitionStateLocked guard, unlike setUint at 2235, so the owner closes ACQUISITIONS_ENABLED in one transaction, anyone drains the queue with the permissionless processAcquisitions, and setUint then succeeds - minutes, not a trap. (2) No NFT or backing is lost or locked; exits unlock the moment the prefix is terminal (_requireExitUnlocked, FWA.sol:1042). Per-purchaser loss is the dust VRF fee (~1e15 wei at 1 gwei), and it is inherited Ethereum-reference behaviour, not a port divergence. (3) Runbook section 6 keeps the frontend read-only and the manifest unpromoted until the canary passes, so the canary is designed to catch exactly this before public exposure. (4) The 998 evidence is a supervised manual drand relayer, not Gelato, so it does not establish that Gelato exceeds 30 blocks - the premise 'systematic failure at launch' is asserted, not shown. The factual core holds. Grep across script/, scripts/, src/, test/ and release/ confirms the ONLY writer of FWAConfigKeys.SELECTION_TIMEOUT_BLOCKS is script/RetryTimedOutDrandGameplayE2E.s.sol:60 (chain-998 path, default 360 from FWA_DRAND_SELECTION_TIMEOUT_BLOCKS). FWA.sol:264 initialises it to 30 and FWA.sol:1373 snapshots block.number + 30. The team's own documents state the required value: FWA_PARITY_MANIFEST.md line 149 ('30 blocs Ethereum deviennent 360 blocs HyperEVM pour conserver environ six minutes') and TESTNET_998_DEPLOYMENTS.md:145-156 (first live 998 request classified TimedOut at 30 blocks, raised to 360). So the gap is real and verified.

Severity is overstated. (a) It fails closed, not open: FWA.sol:1505-1510 -> 1565-1568 -> _creditAcquisitionRefund returns the full escrowed acquisition fee as a pull credit, the NFT stays with its depositor, no custody or accounting invariant breaks. (b) It is not permanent and not irreversible: every affected sequence expires at requestBlock+30 and is immediately processable, so unsettledAcquisitionCount reaches 0 within seconds, at which point the owner's single setUint(SELECTION_TIMEOUT_BLOCKS, 360) succeeds (FWA.sol:2247-2251; the 2235 lock is transient by construction here, and setBool(WITHDRAW_ONLY,true) forces the window deterministically). (c) The 'purchasers lose the full randomness fee' impact is economically negligible: I measured the live HyperEVM mainnet gas price at 0.1 gwei (cast gas-price against https://rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm returned 100000000), so the unrefunded vrfServiceFee is 800000*1e8*13000/10000 = 1.04e14 wei = ~0.0001 HYPE per attempt, not a meaningful loss. Nothing here is a fund/NFT lock-up, permanent settlement DoS, unauthorised admin power, or an irreversible early open, which is what 'high' requires. Correct severity: medium (external-config).

findings.title: Coordinator rotation permanently bricks all acquisitions: GelatoVRFCoordinator restarts request IDs at 1 and FWA rejects reused IDs forever
findings.preconditions: At least one acquisition has been requested through coordinator A (i.e. `acquisitions[1..N]` are populated in FWA), and the owner then points FWA at a freshly deployed coordinator B via `setAddr(FWAConfigKeys.VRF_COORDINATOR, B)`. This is the documented migration path (`MAINNET_RELEASE_RUNBOOK_2026-07-26.md:182`) and it is *mandatory* if the Gelato dedicated sender ever changes, because `OPERATOR` is `immutable` (GelatoVRFCoordinator.sol:41, comment line 40: 'Rotation requires a new coordinator').
findings.scenario: 1) Launch on coordinator A. Users perform 500 acquisitions; FWA stores `acquisitions[1] … acquisitions[500]` with terminal statuses. These entries are never deleted. 2) Gelato rotates the dedicated msg.sender (or the operator key is compromised). The team deploys coordinator B — `nextRequestId` is a hard-coded storage initialiser `= 1` (line 43) with no constructor parameter — drains the queue, and calls `fwa.setAddr(60, B)`. 3) The next `acquire()` runs `requestId = s_vrfCoordinator.requestRandomWords(...)` → B returns 1 (line 113), then FWA.sol:1387 evaluates `acquisitions[1].status != AcquisitionStatus.None` → true → `revert DuplicateRequestId()`. 4) The revert rolls back B's `nextRequestId++`, so B's counter is still 1. Every subsequent attempt repeats forever. There is no escape: `setConsumer` is one-shot (lines 92-97), so B's counter cannot be advanced by pointing it at a throwaway consumer first, and FWA is not upgradeable. On Ethereum this cannot happen because Chainlink derives `requestId = keccak256(keyHash, sender, subId, nonce)` — globally unique across coordinators. The port replaced a globally-unique ID with a per-contract counter without preserving the uniqueness property FWA depends on.
findings.impact: A routine or emergency operator rotation converts into permanent, unrecoverable DoS of the acquisition path on a non-upgradeable core that custodies user NFTs and HYPE. Depositors can still withdraw (exits unlock once the queue drains) but the product is dead and requires a full core redeploy plus manual migration of every custodied NFT. The existing migration test `test/FWADrandRelayIntegration.t.sol:53-79` masks this: it switches coordinators *before* any request has ever been issued, so ID 1 is still free.
findings.minimalFix: Give the coordinator a constructor parameter `uint256 startRequestId` (or an owner-only, pre-`setConsumer` `seedRequestId(uint256)`) and require it to be strictly greater than the outgoing coordinator's `nextRequestId`; the mainnet deploy/rotation script should read the old coordinator and pass `oldNextRequestId + margin`. Alternatively derive `requestId = uint256(keccak256(abi.encode(address(this), block.chainid, localNonce)))` so IDs are globally unique like Chainlink's.
findings.regressionTest: `testRotatingCoordinatorAfterLiveRequestsStillAllowsAcquire`: run one full acquire→fulfil→process cycle on coordinator A, deploy coordinator B, `setAddr(VRF_COORDINATOR, B)`, and assert the next `acquire()` succeeds (does not revert `DuplicateRequestId`) and that B's returned ID does not collide with any populated `acquisitions[id]`.

refutationNotes.reason: MECHANISM CONFIRMED, IMPACT MATERIALLY WRONG. GelatoVRFCoordinator.sol:43 is a hard `uint256 public nextRequestId = 1` with no constructor parameter and no setter; setConsumer (92-97) is one-shot; FWA.sol:1387 reverts DuplicateRequestId on any populated acquisitions[id]; grep confirms FWA never deletes acquisitions entries (only writes at 1391, reads at 1488/1554). The case is genuinely untested: test/FWADrandRelayIntegration.t.sol:53-54 rotates before any request, and TESTNET_998_DEPLOYMENTS.md:172-176 shows the live 998 rotation was also collision-free because PoPRandomnessAdapter never served a request (it still reverts InvalidCaller() behind the provider registration gate). VerifyGelatoVRFCoordinator.s.sol checks no counter. But the impact paragraph does not survive. The failed acquire() reverts ATOMICALLY, so unsettledAcquisitionCount and unfulfilledVrfCount both remain 0, which means setAddr(VRF_COORDINATOR, ...) (FWA.sol:2323-2325) is still callable. Recovery is therefore trivial: point back at coordinator A, or deploy the same peripheral with a seeded counter - a three-line change to a 5 KB non-upgradeable helper that is being redeployed anyway as part of the rotation. There is no 'permanent, unrecoverable DoS', no 'full core redeploy', and no 'manual migration of every custodied NFT'; deposits and withdrawals keep working throughout because unsettled is 0 so _requireExitUnlocked passes. Outage is a self-inflicted, hours-long acquisition pause with zero fund impact. Real latent defect worth the seeded-ID fix, but medium (recoverable), not high.

The defect is real and I reproduced it executably. GelatoVRFCoordinator.sol:43 is a bare storage initialiser `uint256 public nextRequestId = 1;` with no constructor parameter and no seeding path; setConsumer is one-shot (92-97) and requestRandomWords is onlyConsumer (106), so nothing but FWA can advance the counter. FWA.sol:1387-1389 reverts DuplicateRequestId when acquisitions[requestId].status != None, and terminal acquisitions are never deleted. I wrote a probe outside the audited tree (run via FOUNDRY_TEST override, no repo file touched): one full acquire -> fulfil -> keepNFT cycle on coordinator A, then deploy a fresh coordinator B of the same source, setAddr(VRF_COORDINATOR, B), seed the service so coverage is not the blocker, and the next acquire() reverts with exactly FWA.DuplicateRequestId; B's nextRequestId is still 1 afterwards, so it repeats. The premise is also correct that this is the documented path (MAINNET_RELEASE_RUNBOOK_2026-07-26.md:182) and that test/FWADrandRelayIntegration.t.sol:53-79 masks it (it rotates before any request has been issued). All three coordinators in the repo share the pattern (DrandRelayCoordinator.sol:49, PoPRandomnessAdapter.sol:41).

The impact paragraph is materially wrong, which is why severity drops. FWA.sol:2323-2325 stores s_vrfCoordinator as an arbitrary IVRFCoordinatorV2Plus address and only ever calls four selectors; recovery is therefore to deploy a coordinator variant whose IDs start above the highest used id (a one-line change to line 43, or the keccak derivation the finding itself proposes) and issue one setAddr. That is exactly the same operational act the rotation already required. There is NO need for 'a full core redeploy plus manual migration of every custodied NFT'. Nothing is lost, nothing is locked: deposits, withdrawals, settlement, refunds and every pull path keep working throughout, and the failure surfaces on the first acquire after rotation, before any user funds are committed. Trigger frequency is also low (an owner-initiated, planned rotation). Correct severity: medium (contract-bug, fail-closed, recoverable without touching the core).

findings.title: A full reserved activation batch exceeds HyperEVM's 2M small-block gas limit, freezing settlement and every depositor exit
findings.lines: 243-244 (maxActivationsPerAcquisition = 6), 897-933 (_activateListing), 954-987 (_reserveStagedBatch / _activateReservedBatch), 1275, 1327, 1550-1582 (processAcquisitions), 2124-2153 (32-deep tree writes); DeployHyperEVMMainnetCore.s.sol:94-99 (never re-tunes the caps)
findings.preconditions: Chain 999. Six or more `listNFT` deposits land while at least one acquisition is unresolved (the normal case on a live pool — FWA.sol:866 stages every deposit whenever `unsettledAcquisitionCount != 0`), and a subsequent `acquire()` reserves them via `_reserveStagedBatch` (up to `maxActivationsPerAcquisition = 6`, left at the Ethereum default by the mainnet deploy script). The sender processing the queue has not opted into HyperEVM big blocks.
findings.scenario: Measured on this tree with `forge test -vvvv` (all 91 tests pass): a single `_activateListing` into a tree whose upper nodes were just zeroed costs **839,164 gas** (`FWA::activateListings(10)` in `testDepositDuringPendingRequestStagesThenActivates`), and the first `listNFT` costs **1,130,935 gas** — the cost is dominated by 33 SSTOREs per insert down a `TREE_DEPTH = 32` sparse segment tree. `FWA_PARITY_MANIFEST.md:37` records HyperEVM's fast blocks at **2M gas** (big blocks 30M, ~1 minute, opt-in per sender via HyperCore). Concrete sequence: listing L1 is active; purchaser opens sequence 1; six depositors stage L2…L7; a second purchaser opens sequence 2, whose `_reserveStagedBatch(2)` detaches all six. When sequence 2 reaches the head, `processAcquisitions(1)` must run `_activateReservedBatch(2)` — six activations, atomically, with no chunking parameter — plus the selection descent (32 cold SLOADs), `_settleAndRemove` (33 more tree writes), and the rewards hooks. Warm-tree arithmetic gives ≈320k/activation → ≈2.25M; cold (pool just emptied by earlier sequences, exactly the measured 839k case) gives ≈5.4M. Both exceed 2M. The same arithmetic applies to `_drainStaging(count * maxActivationsPerAcquisition)` = up to 30 activations inside one `acquireBatch(5)` (FWA.sol:1327) ≈ 9.6M-25M gas. Note the callback fast path deliberately skips reserved batches (FWA.sol:1533-1535), so this work can only ever run in a standalone public tx.
findings.impact: While the head sequence cannot be included in a small block, `unsettledAcquisitionCount` stays non-zero, so `_requireExitUnlocked` (FWA.sol:1042-1044) makes `withdrawListing`, `updateBacking` and `claimTopSpot` revert for **every** depositor, and no acquisition settles — a protocol-wide freeze of exits and settlement while the contract custodies real NFTs and HYPE. There is no on-chain mitigation during the freeze: `setUint(MAX_ACTIVATIONS_PER_ACQUISITION, …)` itself reverts `AcquisitionStateLocked` while `unsettledAcquisitionCount != 0` (FWA.sol:2235). Recovery depends entirely on someone holding a HyperEVM big-block-enabled sender, a capability that appears nowhere in `MAINNET_RELEASE_RUNBOOK_2026-07-26.md` or the emergency-stop section §8. The staging side has a chunked escape (`activateListings(1)`); the reserved batch has none.
findings.minimalFix: Before enabling acquisitions, set `MAX_ACTIVATIONS_PER_ACQUISITION` to a value whose worst-case (cold-tree) cost provably fits a 2M block — measurement here supports 1, at most 2 — and `MAX_ACQUISITIONS_PER_TX` accordingly; add both to `DeployHyperEVMMainnetCore` and to the `InvalidWiring` predicates of `ActivateHyperEVMMainnet`/`VerifyHyperEVMCore`. Independently, document a standing big-block-enabled operator address for `processAcquisitions` in the runbook and in §8 emergency stop.
findings.regressionTest: `testProcessAcquisitionsFitsHyperEVMSmallBlock`: stage `maxActivationsPerAcquisition` listings behind an in-flight acquisition, force the tree cold (empty the pool first), then assert the gas consumed by `processAcquisitions(1)` (measured with `gasleft()` around the call) is < 2_000_000; and a companion assertion that `acquireBatch(maxAcquisitionsPerTx)` with a full staging queue stays under the same bound.

refutationNotes.reason: CONCLUSION SURVIVES, ARITHMETIC AND IMPACT BOTH WRONG. Structural claims verified: _activateReservedBatch (FWA.sol:972-987) is atomic with no chunking parameter, processAcquisitions' maxCount bounds sequences not activations, the callback fast path skips any head with a reserved batch (1532-1535), and setUint(MAX_ACTIVATIONS_PER_ACQUISITION) is blocked by AcquisitionStateLocked at 2235 during the stall. But the gas model is wrong by roughly 2x. LEAF_BASE = 1<<32 and _addTreeWeight walks node = LEAF_BASE + slot - 1 up to the root, so slots 1..6 share the top 30 of 33 path nodes: one batch touches ~41 distinct tree slots, not 6x33 independent cold paths. My measurements: activateListings activating ONE listing into a zeroed tree = 839,164 gas (the figure the finding quotes), but the SECOND activation with the upper tree already non-zero = 281,717 gas, and inside a single transaction the 30 shared ancestors are warm at 100 gas each. Realistic worst case for six activations plus settlement is ~2.2-2.6M with FWARewardsHyperEVM bound (onListingActivated measured at 99,711), not the claimed 5.4M - still above 2M, so the finding's bottom line holds, but only barely and only in the cold-tree case, and the warm steady state (~1.7M) fits. Impact overstated: the stall is not a permanent freeze. processAcquisitions is permissionless and HyperEVM big-block opt-in is a permissionless per-sender HyperCore flag the team has already used (CONTRACTS_TESTNET_RUNBOOK.md:102, ResumeHyperEVMCore.s.sol:25, TESTNET_998_DEPLOYMENTS.md:46-57), so 'a capability that appears nowhere' is only true of the mainnet runbook. The acquireBatch(5)/30-activation limb is a non-issue: _drainStaging there runs only when unsettledAcquisitionCount == 0, in the caller's own transaction, and the permissionless chunked activateListings(1) drains the queue, so it self-heals. Category is also mislabelled 'contract-bug' against the unmodified reference core; the actual gap is that DeployHyperEVMMainnetCore never re-tunes the Ethereum caps. Medium, not high.

The conclusion survives but the evidence and the reproduction are wrong, and the severity is overstated. I measured all of it with probes run outside the audited tree.

The finding's arithmetic is invalid: it multiplies the single 839,164-gas activation observed in testDepositDuringPendingRequestStagesThenActivates by six. That extrapolation cannot hold, because the 32-node path of _addTreeWeight (FWA.sol:2124-2137, LEAF_BASE = 1<<32) is SHARED between adjacent slots and warm after the first activation in the same transaction; the 839k figure is the single-activation-into-a-fully-zeroed-tree case only. Measured reality: the finding's own concrete sequence (one active listing L1, sequence 1 in flight, six staged L2..L7 reserved by sequence 2, rewards module bound, tree emptied by sequence 1) costs processAcquisitions(1) = 1,888,958 gas - UNDER the 2M small-block limit. The same shape without the rewards module is 1,560,242. In a mature pool (400 active listings, six fragmented free slots) it is only 1,071,458, because every tree node on the path is already non-zero.

However, one reachable state does exceed the limit: pool drained to activeListingCount == 0 by the preceding sequence AND a fragmented LIFO free list (built by releasing separated slots last). That measures processAcquisitions(1) = 2,386,377 gas, above 2,000,000, so the headline claim stands. The 2M/30M dual-block figures come from the team's own verified FWA_PARITY_MANIFEST.md line 37. The supporting mechanics also check out: FWA.sol:1531-1535 skips the fast path when the sequence owns reserved listings, _activateReservedBatch (972-987) has no chunking parameter, setUint is globally locked at 2235 while unsettledAcquisitionCount != 0, and _requireExitUnlocked (1042-1044) does block withdrawListing/updateBacking/claimTopSpot meanwhile.

Severity is overstated for two reasons. First, the freeze is not permanent: processAcquisitions is permissionless, and any sender that has opted into HyperEVM big blocks (30M gas) clears it in one transaction - the team can pre-arrange this, so the true finding is the runbook gap, not an unrecoverable state. Second, the acquireBatch sub-claim is wrong on both number and consequence: I measured acquireBatch(5) draining a 30-deep staging queue at 8,037,122 gas (not 9.6M-25M), and that path only executes when unsettledAcquisitionCount == 0 (FWA.sol:1327), i.e. exits are unlocked and the transaction simply fails for its sender - it cannot freeze anything, and activateListings(k) is available as the chunked pre-drain. Correct severity: medium (recoverable, permissionlessly clearable, and only reachable from a drained + fragmented pool state).

findings.title: Fulfilment enforces no minimum delay: requestConfirmations and requestedAtBlock are recorded and never used, and the mainnet coordinator has no round-availability check at all
findings.preconditions: Chain 999. For the outcome-grinding variant: the executing block's `block.timestamp` lagging wall-clock by roughly 1-3 seconds (proposer clock skew, catch-up after a halt, or backlog replay), which makes the target drand round already published at execution time.
findings.scenario: `Request.requestedAtBlock` (line 34) and `Request.requestConfirmations` (line 36) are written at lines 123/125 and then read nowhere — `fulfillRandomness` (140-168) checks only operator identity, status, and payload hash. The testnet coordinator DOES gate on `block.timestamp < roundTimestamp(round)` (DrandRelayCoordinator.sol:163); the mainnet one does not, so it will accept a word for a drand round that does not yet exist, in the same block as the request.
