But the exploitation scenario is effectively closed: every one of the eight dereferences a configured contract before vm.startBroadcast — token.owner() (DeployNestModules:73, DeployNestPlugin:47, InitializeNestMarket:33, LaunchNestMarket:44), token.pool() (ActivateNestMarket:43, ConfigureNestPool:38), fwa.owner() (BindNestRewards:48, BindSplitterHyperEVM:44) — plus router/splitter code.length checks at DeployNestModules:72. On any chain where those addresses lack bytecode the ABI decode reverts before a single broadcast, so the 'spends deployer funds on an unintended chain' consequence does not materialise. The finding itself concedes this is 'defence-in-depth rather than a direct loss path', which is verbatim the rubric's definition of low, not medium.

Factually correct — I confirmed all eight carry only `if (block.chainid == 999 && !envBool(NEST_MAINNET_DEPLOYMENT_CONFIRMED))` and no inequality check, while DeployHyperEVMMainnetCore.s.sol:54, ActivateHyperEVMMainnet.s.sol:42, DeploySplitterHyperEVM.s.sol:40-42 and DeployNestToken.s.sol:46-48 all use the unconditional form. But the finding's own text concedes 'defence-in-depth rather than a direct loss path', which is the definition of low in the stated rubric, not medium. Each of the eight then hits a state guard on an env-supplied address before any mutation — token.owner()!=deployer at InitializeNestMarket.s.sol:33, LaunchNestMarket.s.sol:44, DeployNestPlugin.s.sol:46, DeployNestModules.s.sol:73; fwa.owner()!=owner at BindNestRewards.s.sol:47 and BindSplitterHyperEVM.s.sol:41 — which on an unintended chain reverts on ABI-decoding a call to a codeless address. Real, cheap, worth fixing; low.

findings.lens: Release sequencing, fail-closed gates and admin powers (main
findings.title: ActivateNestMarket opens public $FWA trading behind NEST_E2E_CONFIRMED, the same flag already required to activate gameplay
findings.preconditions: Final owner is a controlled EOA rather than a Safe - a path the runbook explicitly sanctions in section 6 step 2 ("ou ActivateHyperEVMMainnet.s.sol pour un owner EOA controle"). NEST_E2E_CONFIRMED has been set to true, which is mandatory to run ActivateHyperEVMMainnet at all.
findings.scenario: ActivateHyperEVMMainnet.s.sol:47 requires `vm.envBool("NEST_E2E_CONFIRMED")` before it may open gameplay acquisitions. ActivateNestMarket.s.sol:33 requires the identical `vm.envBool("NEST_E2E_CONFIRMED")` before it calls token.setExternalBuysEnabled(true) (line 58). The other precondition, NEST_MAINNET_DEPLOYMENT_CONFIRMED, has been true since the first mainnet broadcast. Therefore, at the exact moment the operator becomes able to activate gameplay, they are simultaneously able to open public $FWA trading with a single stray command, and no new flag has to be flipped. There is no NEST_PUBLIC_TRADING_CONFIRMED variable anywhere in .env.mainnet.example.
findings.impact: Contradicts MAINNET_RELEASE_RUNBOOK section 7 ("L'ouverture du gameplay ne rend pas automatiquement les buys Nest publics") and NEST_DEPLOYMENT_RUNBOOK section "Controle manuel du trading public" on the EOA path. Public $FWA buys can be opened before liquidity, route, spot display and canary-swap review are complete. The action is reversible via setExternalBuysEnabled(false), but any trades executed in the interval are not, and the pre-open checklist the runbook mandates is bypassed.
findings.minimalFix: Introduce a distinct NEST_PUBLIC_TRADING_CONFIRMED flag in .env.mainnet.example (default false) and require it in ActivateNestMarket.s.sol:33 in addition to (or instead of) NEST_E2E_CONFIRMED. Add `token.externalBuysEnabled() == false` to ActivateHyperEVMMainnet.s.sol's wiring assertion so gameplay activation positively attests that public trading is still closed.
findings.regressionTest: Add a script self-test asserting ActivateNestMarket reverts when NEST_PUBLIC_TRADING_CONFIRMED is false even with NEST_E2E_CONFIRMED true. Add a Solidity test asserting ActivateHyperEVMMainnet reverts InvalidWiring when token.externalBuysEnabled() is already true.

refutationNotes.reason: SURVIVES, severity overstated. The flag collision is real: ActivateNestMarket.s.sol:33 and ActivateHyperEVMMainnet.s.sol:47 both read NEST_E2E_CONFIRMED, and grep confirms no NEST_PUBLIC_TRADING_CONFIRMED anywhere in .env.mainnet.example. But 'a single stray command' overstates it materially: ActivateNestMarket is a separately named forge script that must be invoked with an explicit --broadcast, and it additionally requires the full wiring block at lines 46-55 (fwa.rewards()==rewards, fwa.token()==token, pool plugin/fee/communityFee/tickSpacing all matching) plus vm.addr(OWNER_PRIVATE_KEY)==token.owner(). That last check makes the script unreachable on the Safe path, which runbook section 2 designates as the required owner model ('Safe/timelock chain 999 revu, jamais une cle navigateur de test') and section 7 as the trading-control path — so this only exists on the explicitly secondary EOA path. The action is reversible via setExternalBuysEnabled(false), there is no fund-loss path, and the consequence is a bypassed human checklist. That is low ('hardening, defence in depth'), not medium.

The flag observation is correct (ActivateNestMarket.s.sol:33 and ActivateHyperEVMMainnet.s.sol:47 both read NEST_E2E_CONFIRMED) but the consequence is overstated. The runbook property it claims to contradict is literally true: gameplay activation executes only whitelist.setCollections and fwa.setBool(41,true) (ActivateHyperEVMMainnet.s.sol:79-80) and never touches setExternalBuysEnabled — there is no auto-open. Opening trading requires deliberately invoking a differently named script with OWNER_PRIVATE_KEY and --broadcast; calling that a 'single stray command' is not a plausible operational error. On the mandated final-owner path (runbook section 2: 'Final owner | Safe/timelock chain 999, jamais une cle navigateur de test') the script is unreachable: line 54 requires vm.addr(ownerKey)==token.owner(), which no EOA key satisfies against a Safe, and the contract's own docstring (line 22) says Safe owners must use PrepareMainnetOwnerActions.ps1 instead. NEST_DEPLOYMENT_RUNBOOK's 'Controle manuel du trading public' section documents only the two Safe calldatas. The action is additionally reversible via setExternalBuysEnabled(false). This is flag-granularity hardening: low, not medium.

findings.lens: Release sequencing, fail-closed gates and admin powers (main
findings.title: WriteMainnetManifest emits "links": null on the default configuration, which the frontend manifest schema rejects outright
findings.preconditions: NEST_TRADE_URL is empty - its default in .env.mainnet.example:51 - so the operator invokes WriteMainnetManifest.ps1 without -NestTradeUrl, which is an optional parameter defaulting to "".
findings.scenario: Line 73 is `links = if ($NestTradeUrl) { [ordered]@{ nestTradeUrl = $NestTradeUrl } } else { $null }`. I reproduced the serialization in Windows PowerShell 5.1: the else branch emits the literal JSON member `"links": null`. frontend/src/config/manifest.ts:47-51 declares `links: z.object({ nestTradeUrl: z.string().url().optional() }).optional()`. In zod, .optional() admits undefined but not null; I verified against the project's own zod 4.4.3 that safeParse({links:null}) fails with `Invalid input: expected object, received null` while safeParse({}) succeeds. loadManifest therefore returns { status: "invalid" } (manifest.ts:81-83), and frontend/src/protocol/provider.tsx:240 computes writesEnabled = manifestState.status === "ready" && ... = false. TestReleaseScripts.ps1:20 always passes -NestTradeUrl "https://app.usenest.xyz/fixture", so the null branch is never exercised by the release gate and the defect is invisible until mainnet launch day.
findings.impact: Fails closed, so no funds are at risk, but it is a launch-day outage: the entire mainnet frontend drops to the degraded read-only banner and no user can deposit, acquire, settle, withdraw or claim through the UI, even after PromoteMainnetManifest.ps1 has correctly set writesEnabled/acquisitionsEnabled to true. Recovery requires editing the published JSON and redeploying the frontend under launch pressure.
findings.minimalFix: Omit the key entirely instead of emitting null - build the manifest without `links` and only `$manifest.links = [ordered]@{ nestTradeUrl = $NestTradeUrl }` when the URL is non-empty (or add `| Where-Object` filtering before ConvertTo-Json). Alternatively relax the schema to `.nullish()` in frontend/src/config/manifest.ts:51. Prefer the script-side fix so the schema stays strict.
findings.regressionTest: Extend TestReleaseScripts.ps1 to also generate a manifest with no -NestTradeUrl and assert the produced JSON has no `links` member; add a frontend unit test in manifest.test.ts asserting DeploymentManifestSchema.safeParse succeeds for a manifest with links absent and documenting the null case.

refutationNotes.reason: SURVIVES fully — the strongest item in the set, and I independently reproduced both halves. PowerShell 5.1: the else branch at WriteMainnetManifest.ps1:73 emits the literal member `"links": null` (reproduced with the exact expression). Node against the project's own zod 4.4.3: safeParse({links:null}) fails with 'Invalid input: expected object, received null' while safeParse({}) succeeds. Chain confirmed end to end: manifest.ts:47-51 -> loadManifest 80-83 returns {status:'invalid'} -> provider.tsx:240 writesEnabled=false -> EnvBanner.tsx:32 degraded state. Two facts that strengthen it beyond what the finding claims: (1) PromoteMainnetManifest.ps1:20/39 round-trips the file through ConvertFrom-Json/ConvertTo-Json and preserves the null, so promotion does not repair it; (2) links.nestTradeUrl has exactly ONE consumer in the whole app, ViemProtocolClient.ts:1146 `externalTradeUrl`, a purely cosmetic optional link — so an unused decorative field bricks the entire mainnet write path. TestReleaseScripts.ps1:20 always passes -NestTradeUrl, so the release gate cannot see it, and NEST_TRADE_URL is empty by default at .env.mainnet.example:51. Severity medium is right (deterministic launch-day write-path outage, fails closed, no funds at risk). One correction: the category is wrong — this is a release-script/frontend schema bug, nothing to do with a contract; it should not be filed as 'contract-bug'.

SURVIVES INTACT — the strongest finding in the set, and I reproduced both halves independently on this machine rather than reasoning about them. PowerShell 5.1.26100.8875: `[ordered]@{ links = if ($NestTradeUrl) {...} else { $null } } | ConvertTo-Json` emits the literal member `"links": null` and .Contains('links') returns True, so the key is genuinely present. Against the project's own zod 4.4.3 under frontend/: safeParse({links:null}) fails with exactly the message the finding quotes, 'Invalid input: expected object, received null', while safeParse({}) succeeds. Chain confirmed end to end: -NestTradeUrl is optional and defaults to "" (WriteMainnetManifest.ps1:15), NEST_TRADE_URL ships empty (.env.mainnet.example:51), manifest.ts:80-83 returns status 'invalid', provider.tsx:240 computes writesEnabled=false. TestReleaseScripts.ps1:20 always passes -NestTradeUrl "https://app.usenest.xyz/fixture", so the null branch is never exercised by the release gate — I confirmed the committed fixture at release/script-self-test/mainnet.json contains a populated links object. I also checked for a second schema break in the same pipeline and found none: PromoteMainnetManifest.ps1's ConvertFrom-Json/ConvertTo-Json round trip preserves a single-element `collections` array as a JSON array, so `links` is the sole failure. Medium is defensible (launch-day total UI outage) though it fails closed with no fund impact. One correction: category should be release-script/frontend defect, not 'contract-bug' — no contract is involved.

findings.title: The release gate's indexer step re-renders the testnet subgraph over subgraph.yaml, and render-manifest.mjs never checks manifest chainId against the target network
findings.lines: 11 ("check": "npm run render:testnet && npm run build"; see also indexer/scripts/render-manifest.mjs:7-33)
findings.preconditions: Operator follows MAINNET_RELEASE_RUNBOOK section 5.3 (render:mainnet, build, then goldsky deploy) and at any point afterwards re-runs TestReleaseCandidate.ps1 - for example to re-attest the candidate before the section 6 activation, which the runbook encourages.
findings.scenario: TestReleaseCandidate.ps1:74 runs `npm run check` in indexer/, which is `render:testnet && build`. render-manifest.mjs rewrites indexer/subgraph.yaml from hyperevm-testnet-998.json and, at lines 25-27, deletes and regenerates indexer/src/generated-collections/ from the 998 collection list. There is no marker, no chain assertion and no diff check: after the gate runs, subgraph.yaml on disk is the chain-998 manifest pointing at the 998 FWA address. The runbook's publish command is `goldsky subgraph deploy hwa-hyperevm/1.0.0 --path .`, which reads whatever subgraph.yaml currently says. Separately, render-manifest.mjs validates manifest.contracts.fwa, deployedAtBlock and per-collection deploymentBlock (line 32 even special-cases network === "hyperevm"), but never validates `manifest.chainId`, so rendering the mainnet network from a 998 manifest - or vice versa - raises no error.
findings.impact: A testnet subgraph can be published under the mainnet Goldsky slug and wired into NEXT_PUBLIC_INDEXER_URL. The mainnet frontend would then present chain-998 listings, acquisitions, activity and NFT ownership as if they were mainnet state. Discovery and history are explicitly declared non-authoritative, and the frontend does re-read the core contract for prices and slippage before signing, so this is misleading data rather than direct loss - but it corrupts the ownership index that drives which NFTs a user is offered, and it would be very hard to notice.
findings.minimalFix: Add `if (network === "hyperevm" && manifest.chainId !== 999) throw ...` and the symmetric 998 check at indexer/scripts/render-manifest.mjs:14. Have render-manifest.mjs write the rendered chainId into subgraph.yaml as a comment or into a sibling .rendered-network file, and add a `predeploy` script that refuses to publish when it does not match the intended target. Change TestReleaseCandidate.ps1:74 to run the render in a temp directory, or restore the previous subgraph.yaml in the finally block.
findings.regressionTest: Add an indexer test that runs render-manifest.mjs with (998 manifest, "hyperevm") and asserts it throws. Add a PowerShell assertion in TestReleaseScripts.ps1 that indexer/subgraph.yaml is byte-identical before and after `npm run check`.

refutationNotes.reason: SURVIVES on the facts, severity overstated, trigger unsupported. Verified: indexer/package.json:11 `"check": "npm run render:testnet && npm run build"`, invoked by TestReleaseCandidate.ps1:74; render-manifest.mjs validates contracts.fwa (line 15), deployedAtBlock (16), and per-collection deploymentBlock (32, special-cased on network==="hyperevm") but never manifest.chainId; lines 25-27 rm -rf and regenerate src/generated-collections. A 'check' that mutates a publishable artefact is a genuine footgun. However the stated trigger is not supported by the document it cites: the gate is runbook section 3 and runs BEFORE section 5.3's render:mainnet -> build -> deploy, and section 6 step 1 lists attestations ('Confirmer source, Gelato task/Gas Tank, Nest E2E ferme et indexeur') — it does not encourage re-running TestReleaseCandidate. Impact is also confined to the layer the architecture explicitly declares non-authoritative: the subgraph is discovery/history only, the frontend re-reads the core before signing, a mis-rendered manifest would carry a visible `network: hyperevm-testnet` in the deployed YAML, and any deposit built on a wrong ownership index simply reverts in ERC721.transferFrom. No fund impact -> 'misleading UI/telemetry with no fund impact' = low.

Both factual claims verified: indexer/package.json:11 is `"check": "npm run render:testnet && npm run build"`, TestReleaseCandidate.ps1:74 runs it, render-manifest.mjs writes subgraph.yaml (line 83) and rm -rf's/regenerates src/generated-collections (25-27), and indexer/subgraph.yaml on disk right now reads `network: hyperevm-testnet` at lines 9 and 81 — the tree is in exactly the state described. render-manifest.mjs validates contracts.fwa (14), deployedAtBlock (15-17) and per-collection deploymentBlock for network==='hyperevm' (32-34) but never manifest.chainId; the two-line fix is correct. Severity should be low, not medium: the finding itself concedes 'misleading data rather than direct loss', the subgraph is declared discovery/history only, a wrong ownership index fails closed at the contract (a deposit by a non-owner reverts on transferFrom), and reaching the bad state requires deploying to Goldsky out of the documented section 5.3 order (render:mainnet, build, deploy) with no re-render in between.

findings.title: Emergency stop has no pre-generated Safe calldata and cannot close the user-facing UI, because FWA.acquisitionsEnabled has no public getter and the frontend gate is the static manifest
findings.preconditions: An incident occurs after activation. Final owner is a Safe. The published manifest has already been promoted with acquisitionsEnabled: true.
findings.scenario: Runbook section 8 lists the emergency sequence as: close ACQUISITIONS_ENABLED, close externalBuysEnabled, pull the public manifest. PrepareMainnetOwnerActions.ps1 pre-generates and reviews calldata for preActivation, the two activation calls, and manualTradingControls.open/close - but nothing to close acquisitions and nothing to set WITHDRAW_ONLY (key 42). Step 1 of the emergency runbook therefore requires signers to hand-encode setBool(41,false) under time pressure, with no reviewed artefact. Second, and independently: FWA.sol:281 declares `bool internal acquisitionsEnabled` with no public accessor anywhere in the contract, so neither PromoteMainnetManifest.ps1 nor the frontend can read it. ViemProtocolClient.ts:1257 gates the acquire() write on `this.manifest.features.acquisitionsEnabled` - the static JSON - and line 466 derives the displayed state the same way. The on-chain reads at lines 1261-1264 cover price and weighted backing only. Consequently an on-chain emergency close does not propagate to the UI at all: the site keeps advertising acquisitions as open and keeps letting users submit and pay gas for transactions that revert AcquisitionsNotEnabled, until a human rebuilds and redeploys the frontend with a re-promoted manifest.
findings.impact: Emergency response is slower and partially manual exactly when it matters. Users lose gas on doomed acquisitions and receive no accurate signal during an incident. No user funds are trapped (FWA.sol:1357 shows acquisitionsEnabled gates only _validateAcquisition; withdrawals, settlements, refunds, finalizeUnsettled and recoverStuckNFT are unaffected, which I verified), so this is misleading state plus operational drag rather than a fund-loss path.
findings.minimalFix: Add an `emergency` section to PrepareMainnetOwnerActions.ps1 emitting reviewed calldata for setBool(41,false), setBool(42,true) (withdraw-only) and setExternalBuysEnabled(false), so the incident path is pre-signed-reviewable. For the UI, have ViemProtocolClient probe the live gate instead of trusting the manifest - e.g. simulateContract on acquire() and surface an AcquisitionsNotEnabled revert as the disabled state, or index the ConfigSet(41, value) event (FWA.sol:2311 emits it) in the subgraph and read the latest value. Note also that the disabled-state message at ViemProtocolClient.ts:1258 is hardcoded to "The supervised drand relayer session is not open", which is a testnet-998 string that would be shown to mainnet users.
findings.regressionTest: Add a frontend test that mocks a manifest with acquisitionsEnabled: true against a core whose acquire() reverts AcquisitionsNotEnabled and asserts the UI renders the closed state rather than offering the action. Add a PowerShell assertion in TestReleaseScripts.ps1 that the generated owner-actions JSON contains a non-empty `emergency` section with the setBool(41,false) selector.

refutationNotes.reason: SURVIVES in reduced form, severity overstated, one impact limb refuted outright. Verified: PrepareMainnetOwnerActions.ps1:28-69 emits only preActivation, the two activation calls and manualTradingControls — no setBool(41,false), no setBool(42,true); FWA.sol:281 `bool internal acquisitionsEnabled` has no accessor anywhere in the contract (grep over the whole file returns only the internal declaration and its four internal uses); ViemProtocolClient.ts:466-467 and 1257 gate on this.manifest.features.acquisitionsEnabled; the hardcoded 'The supervised drand relayer session is not open.' at 1258 is indeed a testnet-998 string on a mainnet build. The user gets a correct message and spends nothing. What remains: no reviewed emergency calldata section, a stale 'open' badge until the manifest is republished, and a testnet string leaking into mainnet copy. All three are UX/operational with no fund impact = low.

All mechanical claims verified. acquisitionsEnabled is `bool internal` at FWA.sol:281 with no accessor anywhere in the contract — I enumerated every reference (281, 1357, 1447, 2299, 2356) and every public bool (only retainedToProtocol at 357 and the derived canRescueRewards() at 2361). findings.title: Crown flag is never indexed for immediately-activated listings because TopListingSet precedes NFTListed
findings.preconditions: A deposit that activates immediately — `unsettledAcquisitionCount == 0 && stagingHead == 0` in `_createListing` (FWA_ETHEREUM_REFERENCE/FWA/sources/src/FWA.sol:866-868) — and that takes or seizes the top. This is unconditionally true for the first listing in an empty pool.
findings.scenario: `_activateListing` (FWA.sol:898-932) runs the top take/seize *before* emitting `NFTListed`: line 921-928 calls `_setTop(listingId)` (which emits `TopListingSet(listingId, depositor)` at FWA.sol:2077-2080), and only then line 932 emits `NFTListed`. On the immediate-activation path no `ListingStaged` was emitted, so at the time `handleTopListingSet` runs there is no `Listing` entity yet: `Listing.load(listingKey(id))` at mapping.ts:475 returns null and `isCrown = true` is silently skipped (mapping.ts:476-479). `handleNFTListed` then creates the entity with `listing.isCrown = false` (mapping.ts:148) and no later event ever revisits it. Concrete values: genesis deposit, `listNFT(0x0ACD…, 1)` with 1 HYPE backing → listingId 1 → `TopListingSet(1, depositor)` at logIndex k, `NFTListed(1, …)` at logIndex k+1 → indexed `Listing["1"].isCrown == false` while `ProtocolState.currentTopListing == "1"`. The index is internally self-contradictory and never converges.
findings.impact: Every crown surface driven by the index is wrong for the genesis listing and for any top seizure that happens while the pool is quiet: `ListingCard.tsx:121,194`, `FeedRow.tsx:38`, `HeroPrizeStack.tsx:310,340`, `ListingDetailDrawer.tsx:101`, `PurchaseResultSurface.tsx:51` ("GRADE CROWN"), and `PositionsScreen.tsx:161` ("♛ crown — pot accrues to this position"). In indexed mode `isCrown` is 100% indexer-derived — `getListing` always returns `isCrown: false` (ViemProtocolClient.ts:513) and `hydrateIndexedListing` overwrites it with the indexed row (ViemProtocolClient.ts:214). A `getListings({view:"top"})` query (`where: { isCrown: true }`, ViemProtocolClient.ts:603) returns an empty set. No fund impact: `claimable.crownPot` uses on-chain `topListingId`/`topListingPot` (ViemProtocolClient.ts:868-869, 899-900), so the pot is still claimable — but the depositor is never told they hold it.
findings.minimalFix: In `handleTopListingSet`, do not depend on the `Listing` entity already existing: record the pending crown on `ProtocolState` (already done via `currentTopListing`) and, in `handleNFTListed`/`handleListingStaged`, set `listing.isCrown = state.currentTopListing == listingKey(id)` instead of hard-coding `false` at mapping.ts:148 / 118. Equivalent alternative: in `handleTopListingSet`, when the entity is absent, defer by leaving `currentTopListing` set and reconciling on the next listing write.
findings.regressionTest: Matchstick test: fire `TopListingSet(1, depositor)` then `NFTListed(1, slot=0, depositor, collection, tokenId, weight, value)` in that log order (never the reverse) and assert both `Listing["1"].isCrown == true` and `ProtocolState["protocol"].currentTopListing == "1"`. Add a general invariant assertion to the suite: `currentTopListing != null` implies `Listing[currentTopListing].isCrown == true`.

refutationNotes.reason: Ordering confirmed in the parity oracle: FWA.sol:921-929 calls _setTop, which emits TopListingSet at FWA.sol:2078-2081, and NFTListed is emitted only afterwards at FWA.sol:932; the immediate-activation branch (FWA.sol:866-868) emits no ListingStaged, so Listing.load at mapping.ts:475 returns null, the isCrown=true write is skipped, and handleNFTListed then hard-codes isCrown=false at mapping.ts:148. The staged path is unaffected (the entity exists, and handleNFTListed only sets isCrown=false when it creates the entity). Real, but the impact is cosmetic and smaller than claimed: grep shows `view: "top"` is referenced only in types.ts:451 and the two client branches (ViemProtocolClient.ts:581,603) — no component ever issues that query, so the 'empty top view' consequence is unreachable. The crown pot is unaffected (getUserPositions computes crownPot from on-chain topListingId/topListingPot at lines 899-900, and the listing IS present in the indexed set, just with the wrong flag). What remains is a wrong badge/label on cards and one Positions line. Under this rubric that is 'misleading UI with no fund impact' = low.

Ordering confirmed in the parity core: _activateListing calls _setTop at FWA.sol:921-928 (which emits TopListingSet at FWA.sol:2077-2080) and only then emits NFTListed at FWA.sol:932; the immediate-activation branch at FWA.sol:866-868 emits no ListingStaged, so handleTopListingSet's `Listing.load` at mapping.ts:475 returns null and the isCrown write at 476-479 is skipped, after which handleNFTListed hard-codes `listing.isCrown = false` at mapping.ts:148 and nothing revisits it (handleTopListingSet:462-468 only ever clears the old crown). I confirmed the staged path is unaffected — the entity already exists, and handleNFTListed only sets isCrown inside the `listing == null` branch. Frontend coupling is as described: getListing returns `isCrown: false` (ViemProtocolClient.ts:513), hydrateIndexedListing overwrites from the row (210), and view:"top" filters on `isCrown: true` (603). But severity is one notch too high. This rubric's `medium` is recoverable griefing, incorrect accounting, or a gate failing open; this is none of those and the finding itself states "No fund impact". I verified the crown pot needs no user awareness at all: _vacateTop credits `feeCredit[depositor] += pot` automatically (FWA.sol:2060-2073) and getUserPositions derives claimable.crownPot from the on-chain topListingId/topListingPot (ViemProtocolClient.ts:868-869, 899-900), so a depositor who is never shown the crown still sees and claims the money. That is exactly "misleading UI with no fund impact" = low.

findings.lens: Indexer (Goldsky subgraph) correctness and its consumption b
findings.title: EnvBanner never warns on indexer status "down", only on "lagging"
findings.preconditions: `getConnectionHealth()` returns `indexer.status === "down"`, which it does both when the GraphQL request fails (ViemProtocolClient.ts:701-702) and — critically — when the subgraph reports `hasIndexingErrors: true` (ViemProtocolClient.ts:695).
findings.scenario: The banner chain is `if (health?.rpc === "down") {…} else if (health && health.indexer.status === "lagging") {…}`. There is no branch for `"down"`. So the ordering of severity is inverted: a subgraph that is merely 25 blocks behind produces a visible amber banner ("Indexer 25 blocks behind"), while a subgraph that has *failed with indexing errors* — the state in which the Positions screen, the reveal queue and the owned-NFT list are silently empty — produces no banner at all. Concrete sequence: the subgraph traps on the missing ERC721 ABI, Goldsky reports `hasIndexingErrors: true`, `getConnectionHealth` returns `status: "down"`, `EnvBanner` renders `null` (line 63), and the user sees a normal-looking app with an empty portfolio. Only `ActivityScreen.tsx:149-153` handles `"down"`, and only in its empty state; `PositionsScreen` does not call `useConnectionHealth` at all.
findings.impact: The health signal that the README advertises as the trust boundary ("`_meta.block.number` is compared with the RPC head and lag is visible in UI", indexer/README.md:46) fails open in its most dangerous state. This is the amplifier that turns a stalled subgraph into a missed settlement window: the user has no reason to suspect the displayed portfolio is incomplete.
findings.minimalFix: Add an explicit `down` branch before the `lagging` branch, e.g. `else if (health && health.indexer.status === "down") { items.push({ tone: "red", text: "Indexer unavailable — positions, history and the reveal may be incomplete; act from the explorer if a settlement window is running", testid: "banner-indexer-down" }); }`. Also surface the health state on PositionsScreen and in the deposit flow's owned-NFT list, not only on ActivityScreen.
findings.regressionTest: React Testing Library test for `EnvBanner`: mock `useConnectionHealth` to return `{ rpc: "ok", indexer: { status: "down", lagBlocks: 0, indexedBlock: 0n, chainBlock: 100n } }` and assert `getByTestId("banner-indexer-down")` is present. Add the symmetric case for `hasIndexingErrors: true` in the `getConnectionHealth` unit test to pin the `down` mapping.

refutationNotes.reason: Confirmed: EnvBanner.tsx:47-59 branches on rpc==="down" then indexer.status==="lagging" and returns null at line 61 otherwise; ActivityScreen.tsx:149-153 is the only "down" consumer and PositionsScreen imports only usePoolSnapshot/usePositions (line 11), never useConnectionHealth. But the finding misses why the branch is hard to add and mis-specifies the fix: getConnectionHealth also returns indexer.status "down" when no indexer is configured at all (ViemProtocolClient.ts:683-684) and on any transient query failure (line 701-702), so the proposed unconditional red 'Indexer unavailable — act from the explorer' banner would fire permanently in every direct-read deployment and on every blip. The real defect is that "down" conflates not-configured, transient-failure and failed-with-indexing-errors into one value. Impact is telemetry only, no fund path — low.

Refuted on its central factual claim. The finding's concrete sequence ends "EnvBanner renders null (line 63), and the user sees a normal-looking app with an empty portfolio", and asserts "Only ActivityScreen.tsx:149-153 handles down". That is wrong. TopBar.tsx:28-36 — rendered immediately above EnvBanner on every route by AppShell.tsx:22-23 — contains `if (health.indexer.status === "down") return { dot: "bg-red", label: "Indexer down", tone: "text-red" };` ahead of the lagging branch. A subgraph with hasIndexingErrors: true therefore produces a persistent red "Indexer down" chip in the sticky navbar on the Positions screen, the pool and the deposit flow — arguably more visible than the 28px slim banner the finding wants, and certainly not "no banner at all". The claimed severity inversion (lagging louder than down) does not exist once TopBar is accounted for: down is red, lagging is amber. There is also a concrete design reason the branch is absent from EnvBanner specifically: getConnectionHealth returns `status: "down"` for `!this.indexerUrl` too (ViemProtocolClient.ts:686-688), so the proposed red banner ("Indexer unavailable — positions, history and the reveal may be incomplete") would fire permanently in every intentional no-indexer/direct-mode deployment. Adding a second surface for the same signal is a UI preference, not a defect that fails open.

findings.lens: Indexer (Goldsky subgraph) correctness and its consumption b
findings.title: Pool odds distribution is computed over a 200-row indexer window and renormalised to 100%
findings.preconditions: More than 200 active listings in the pool, and `NEXT_PUBLIC_INDEXER_URL` set. No attacker required.
findings.scenario: `PoolScreen.tsx:54` requests `useListings({ view: "pool", sort: "value", direction: "desc", limit: 250 })`. In the indexed path, `getIndexedListings` computes `scanSize = Math.min(200, Math.max(query.limit * 4, query.limit + 1))` = `Math.min(200, 1000)` = **200** (line 615) and never paginates further, so `poolAll.items` is capped at the 200 highest-`backing` active listings. `HeroStatsBar` (PoolScreen.tsx:308-323) then computes the headline strip labelled "Chance an acquisition lands on a <tier> position" by summing weights over that subset and dividing by `total = Σ weights of the subset` (line 318-321) — not by the on-chain `snapshot.totalWeight`. Because FWA weight is inverse to backing (`weight = INVERSE_WEIGHT_NUMERATOR / value`, FWA.sol:1114), ordering by `backing` desc selects exactly the *lowest-weight*, lowest-probability listings, then renormalises them to 100%. Concrete values: 600 active listings, the top 200 by backing carrying 8% of total weight and all falling in the "common" band → the strip renders "Common 100.0%" while the true grail/epic probability mass is entirely invisible. The direct (no-indexer) path does not truncate this way (`getListings` slices to `query.limit` over the full enumeration, line 596), so mock/testnet and mainnet disagree.
findings.impact: The probability breakdown displayed immediately above the buy panel misrepresents the odds of the paid, irreversible draw the user is about to sign. No funds are stolen, but the headline decision input is wrong and the error grows with pool size — i.e. it appears only after launch succeeds.
findings.minimalFix: Do not derive pool-wide aggregates from a paginated listing page. Either (a) add a `RarityBand`/weight-histogram aggregate entity to `schema.graphql` maintained in the mapping and query it directly, or (b) normalise by `snapshot.totalWeight` (on-chain) instead of the subset sum and render an explicit "top 200 shown" qualifier, or (c) have `getIndexedListings` honour `limit > scanSize` by paging until `limit` rows are collected. Option (a) is the only one that stays correct at scale.
findings.regressionTest: Vitest on `getIndexedListings`: stub the indexer to return 200 rows for `limit: 250` and assert either `page.items.length === 250` or that the returned page carries an explicit truncation marker. Plus a component test for `HeroStatsBar` passing 200 listings whose summed weight is 8% of `snapshot.totalWeight`, asserting the rendered percentages are relative to `snapshot.totalWeight` (sum ≈ 8%), not renormalised to 100%.

refutationNotes.reason: Arithmetic confirmed: PoolScreen.tsx:54 asks for limit 250, getIndexedListings computes scanSize = Math.min(200, Math.max(1000, 251)) = 200 (line 615) and never pages further, and HeroStatsBar divides by the subset sum at PoolScreen.tsx:318-321. Weight is indeed inverse to backing (FWA.sol:178, 819), so sorting by backing desc selects the lowest-probability rows. Two corrections that reduce it. (a) The claimed mock/mainnet divergence does not hold: the direct path slices to query.limit=250 over an enumeration itself hard-bounded at 1,000 listings (MAX_ENUMERATED_LISTINGS, line 527) and feeds the same renormalising component, so the defect is path-independent and only the cut-off differs (200 vs 250) — the bug is in HeroStatsBar, not primarily in scanSize. (b) The per-listing tier assignment is already correct (rarityFromOdds against snapshot.totalWeight, PoolScreen.tsx:315); only the headline percentage is renormalised. The condition is also already tracked in-tree by the comment at PoolScreen.tsx:52-53 pointing at INTEGRATION_NEEDS, and sits adjacent to the disclosed 'bounded window, approximate totals' limit. Misleading UI, no fund impact — low.

The mechanism is confirmed: PoolScreen.tsx:54 requests limit 250 for the distribution strip, getIndexedListings computes `scanSize = Math.min(200, Math.max(250*4, 251)) = 200` (ViemProtocolClient.ts:615) with no further paging, and HeroStatsBar (PoolScreen.tsx:308-323) divides each tier's summed weight by `total`, the subset sum at line 318-321, rather than by the on-chain snapshot.totalWeight it already holds. The worked example is inverted, however, and materially so. rarityFromOdds computes `oneIn = totalWeight / weight` with grail at oneIn > 600 (frontend/src/protocol/rarity.ts:8-16), and weight is `INVERSE_WEIGHT_NUMERATOR / value` (FWA.sol:819). Ordering by backing desc therefore selects the *highest* oneIn — the grail/epic end, not the common band. The strip would render something like "Grail 90% / Epic 10%", i.e. it overstates the chance of a grail rather than showing "Common 100.0%". Scope is also narrower than stated: with 200 or fewer active listings the subset is the whole active pool and the strip is exact, so this cannot bite at launch, and the tier assignment itself is always correct because it uses snapshot.totalWeight. PoolScreen.tsx:52-53 already carries an in-code acknowledgement that this should be an indexer aggregate. Real defect worth fixing, but "misleading UI/telemetry with no fund impact" = low.

findings.lens: Indexer (Goldsky subgraph) correctness and its consumption b
findings.title: render-manifest.mjs keys its mainnet completeness guard on the CLI network string, not on the manifest chainId
findings.preconditions: An operator renders the mainnet manifest with any `<graph-network>` argument other than the literal string `hyperevm`, or supplies a `deploymentBlock` later than a collection's first mint.
findings.scenario: The only guard that forces complete ERC-721 ownership indexing is `if (network === "hyperevm" && !Number.isSafeInteger(collection.deploymentBlock)) throw …` (lines 32-34). It depends entirely on a positional CLI argument. `render-manifest.mjs ../frontend/public/deployments/hyperevm-mainnet-999.json hyperevm-mainnet` — a natural typo, since it matches the manifest *filename* — silently takes the else branch: `startBlock = collection.deploymentBlock ?? manifest.deployedAtBlock` (line 31) falls back to the FWA deployment block for every collection. Nothing cross-checks `manifest.chainId` (999, present in the manifest and validated nowhere in this script) against the network name, and nothing checks that the mainnet manifest is not being rendered onto `hyperevm-testnet` or vice versa. Two further gaps on the non-mainnet path: `collection.deploymentBlock` is interpolated raw into YAML at line 43 with no type or sign check (a negative or non-numeric value reaches the manifest; the top-level `deployedAtBlock` does get a `< 0` check at line 15, collections do not), and even on the mainnet path `Number.isSafeInteger` does not verify the block precedes the collection's first mint.
findings.impact: Ownership indexing starting after the first mint yields an `OwnedToken` set that omits every token that has not moved since the FWA deployment block — i.e. most holders. `getIndexedOwnedEligibleNFTs` (ViemProtocolClient.ts:1023-1037) is the sole source of the deposit flow's wallet inventory in indexed mode, so eligible holders are told they own nothing and cannot deposit. This is exactly the failure the README claims the guard prevents (indexer/README.md:26-28), enforced only by a shell argument — a gate that fails open under a plausible operational error.
findings.minimalFix: Derive the graph network from the manifest instead of trusting argv, or at minimum cross-validate: `const expected = manifest.chainId === 999 ? "hyperevm" : manifest.chainId === 998 ? "hyperevm-testnet" : null; if (expected === null || expected !== network) throw new Error(...)`. Then key the completeness guard on `manifest.chainId === 999`. Additionally validate every `collection.deploymentBlock` with `Number.isSafeInteger(v) && v >= 0` on all networks before interpolating it at line 43, and require `deploymentBlock <= manifest.deployedAtBlock` (a collection allowlisted at launch must predate the core).
findings.regressionTest: Node test over `render-manifest.mjs`: (1) a chainId-999 manifest with `hyperevm-testnet` as the network argument must throw; (2) a chainId-999 manifest whose collection lacks `deploymentBlock` must throw for every network argument, not just `hyperevm`; (3) a collection with `deploymentBlock: -1` must throw. Assert against a temp manifest so the repo's rendered `subgraph.yaml` is untouched.

refutationNotes.reason: The code reads exactly as described (render-manifest.mjs:32-34 gates on `network === "hyperevm"`), but the scenario is not a plausible operational error, which is what the medium rating rests on. The operator never types the network argument: package.json pins `"render:mainnet": "node scripts/render-manifest.mjs ../frontend/public/deployments/hyperevm-mainnet-999.json hyperevm"`, and indexer/README.md:30-33 documents `npm run render:mainnet` as the mainnet path. For the 'natural typo' to reach production the operator would have to bypass the pinned script AND choose a network string that graph-cli and Goldsky both accept for deployment — 'hyperevm-mainnet' is not a supported network name, so the run fails loudly at deploy rather than silently producing a partial ownership index. The sub-claims degenerate similarly: a negative or non-numeric collection.deploymentBlock interpolated at line 43 yields a manifest that fails validation at build/deploy, not a wrong index. Deriving the network from manifest.chainId and range-checking deploymentBlock are worthwhile hardening (info), but this is not a gate that fails open under a plausible error.

The core observation is correct — the completeness guard at render-manifest.mjs:32-34 tests `network === "hyperevm"`, a positional argv value, and never reads manifest.chainId, while startBlock silently falls back to manifest.deployedAtBlock at line 31. The sub-claim about weak numeric validation is also right, and slightly stronger than stated: Number.isSafeInteger(-1) is true, so a negative deploymentBlock passes even the mainnet guard and reaches the raw YAML interpolation at line 43. But the operational premise that makes it `medium` ("a gate that fails open under a plausible operational error") does not hold up. Both documented invocations hardcode the pairing — package.json line 8 defines `render:mainnet` as `... hyperevm-mainnet-999.json hyperevm`, and MAINNET_RELEASE_RUNBOOK_2026-07-26.md:112-115 runs `npm run render:mainnet`, not the raw node command. Producing the described typo requires abandoning both. I also checked the bundled Graph networks registry (node_modules/@graphprotocol/graph-cli/config/TheGraphNetworksRegistry.json, 156 networks) and it contains no hyperevm entry at all, so network naming is validated only by the deploy backend — meaning an invented name like `hyperevm-mainnet` is far more likely to be rejected at `goldsky subgraph deploy` than to quietly ship an incomplete ownership index. Worth hardening (derive the network from chainId, validate deploymentBlock >= 0), but low.

findings.lens: FWA core, parity and liability conservation (HyperEVM mainne
findings.title: First mainnet acquire() reverts InsufficientVrfCoverage: FWAVRFService coverage is ~20x the purchaser fee at HyperEVM gas prices and nothing pre-funds it
findings.preconditions: Mainnet values from `.env.mainnet.example`: `FWA_MIN_RANDOMNESS_BUFFER_WEI = 1e16`, `FWA_MAX_RANDOMNESS_COST_WEI = 1e16`, `FWA_RANDOMNESS_GAS_ESTIMATE = 800000`, `FWA_RANDOMNESS_MARGIN_BPS = 3000`, `FWA_RANDOMNESS_FLAT_WEI = 0`. `FWAVRFService` holds no HYPE after deployment and the runbook's funding step (§5.1) funds only the Gelato Gas Tank.
findings.scenario: The canary purchaser calls `acquire{value: fee + vrf}`. FWA computes `vrf = vrfServiceFee() = 800000 * tx.gasprice * 13000/10000` (FWAVRFService.sol:191-193). At a HyperEVM gas price of ~1 gwei that is ≈1.04e15 wei (0.00104 HYPE). FWA then calls `prepareRequests{value: vrf}(1)`, which runs `_ensureSubscriptionCoverage(1)`: `required = minimumSubscriptionBuffer + (unfulfilledVrfCount + 1) * maxFulfillmentCostWei = 1e16 + 1*1e16 = 2e16` (0.02 HYPE). `current = coordinator.nativeSubscriptionBalance = 0`, so `amount = 2e16`, and `if (amount > address(this).balance) revert InsufficientVrfCoverage()` fires because the service holds only the 0.00104 HYPE just received. Every acquisition reverts until someone sends ≥0.02 HYPE (≥0.06 HYPE to support `acquireBatch(5)`) to the service. This never surfaced on 998 because `.env.example:23-24` sets both coverage values to **1 wei**, disabling the check entirely.
findings.impact: Fails closed, so no funds are lost, but the first real user transaction on a live mainnet product reverts with an opaque error and the canary in runbook §6 cannot complete. Secondary issue: the coverage ETH that is eventually moved is sent to `GelatoVRFCoordinator.fundSubscriptionWithNative`, a pure bookkeeping sink — Gelato executions are actually paid from the off-chain Gas Tank — and `withdrawNative` requires `pendingRequestCount == 0` (GelatoVRFCoordinator.sol:206-213), so purchaser fees accumulate as dead reserve. Lowering `maxFulfillmentCostWei` later is possible only by first closing acquisitions, because `setCoverageConfig` enforces `maxFulfillmentCost >= requestConfigCoverageFloor` (FWAVRFService.sol:331) and `_setCoverageConfig` reverts `OutstandingCallbacks` while any callback is in flight.
findings.minimalFix: Re-derive the coverage parameters for HyperEVM gas prices (the Gelato coordinator consumes no on-chain subscription balance, so `FWA_MAX_RANDOMNESS_COST_WEI` should reflect the real per-callback charge, not an Ethereum-scale 0.01 ETH), and add an explicit seed-funding step plus a pre-activation assertion `address(service).balance >= service.requiredSubscriptionBalance(fwa.maxAcquisitionsPerTx())` to `ActivateHyperEVMMainnet.s.sol` and `VerifyHyperEVMCore.s.sol`.
findings.regressionTest: `testFirstAcquireSucceedsWithMainnetCoverageParameters`: construct `FWAVRFService(1e16, 1e16)` with `setFeeConfig(800000, 3000, 0)` and a realistic `vm.txGasPrice(1 gwei)`, wire the mainnet coordinator, and assert `acquire()` succeeds from a zero-balance service — it must fail today with `InsufficientVrfCoverage`, and pass once the seeding assertion is added to the deploy path.

refutationNotes.reason: FACTS CONFIRMED AND STRONGER THAN CLAIMED. .env.mainnet.example:28-29 sets both coverage values to 1e16 while .env.example:23-24 sets both to 1 wei, so the check is effectively disabled on 998 and armed on 999. requiredSubscriptionBalance (FWAVRFService.sol:210-214) = 1e16 + (0+1)*1e16 = 2e16; subscriptionNativeBalance reads GelatoVRFCoordinator.nativeSubscriptionBalance = 0; _ensureSubscriptionCoverage:250 reverts because address(this).balance is only the ~1.04e15 requestFee just received (break-even needs ~19 gwei, far above HyperEVM). Decisive corroboration the finding missed: script/PrepareDrandGameplayE2E.s.sol:134-142 implements exactly the missing _prefundCoverage step for 998, and there is no mainnet equivalent; no test asserts InsufficientVrfCoverage anywhere. SEVERITY OVERSTATED. It fails closed, loses nothing, and is cured by a single HYPE transfer to the service's receive() - or by anyone calling the unpermissioned coordinator.fundSubscriptionWithNative. Runbook section 6 step 4 is precisely the transaction that would surface it, while the frontend is still read-only. It also self-corrects: purchaser fees accumulate in the service, so after ~20 acquisitions coverage is met without intervention. The 'dead reserve' sub-claim is overstated: withdrawNative (GelatoVRFCoordinator.sol:206-213) only blocks while pendingRequestCount != 0, which is the normal idle state between acquisitions, so the owner can retrieve it. Fails closed with no fund impact = low, not medium.

Confirmed executably, and the finding actually understates how certain the failure is. FWAVRFService.sol:210-214 computes required = minimumSubscriptionBuffer + (unfulfilledVrfCount + additional) * maxFulfillmentCostWei, and 242-255 reverts InsufficientVrfCoverage when required - current exceeds address(this).balance. With the exact .env.mainnet.example values (FWA_MIN_RANDOMNESS_BUFFER_WEI=1e16, FWA_MAX_RANDOMNESS_COST_WEI=1e16, FWA_RANDOMNESS_GAS_ESTIMATE=800000, FWA_RANDOMNESS_MARGIN_BPS=3000, FWA_RANDOMNESS_FLAT_WEI=0) my probe shows the first acquire() reverting with exactly FWAVRFService.InsufficientVrfCoverage, and succeeding once the service is seeded - so the mechanism and the missing seeding step are both real. I also confirmed the 998 masking claim: .env.example sets both coverage values to 1 wei. And I confirmed no seed step exists anywhere: the runbook's only funding instruction is section 5.1 (Gelato Gas Tank), and neither ActivateHyperEVMMainnet nor VerifyHyperEVMCore asserts service balance.

One correction, in the finding's disfavour: the '~20x' estimate assumes 1 gwei. I queried the live chain read-only (cast gas-price against https://rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm) and HyperEVM mainnet returns 100000000 wei = 0.1 gwei. requestFee is therefore 800000 * 1e8 * 13000/10000 = 1.04e14 wei against a required 2e16 - a ~192x shortfall, not 20x. The first acquire is not marginal, it is guaranteed to revert, and roughly 192 purchaser fees would be needed to self-fund the buffer. The secondary observations also hold: GelatoVRFCoordinator.fundSubscriptionWithNative (198-204) is a pure bookkeeping sink, withdrawNative (206-213) is blocked while pendingRequestCount != 0, and FWAVRFService.sol:331 / 369-379 make lowering the coverage later conditional on the floor and on zero outstanding callbacks. Severity medium is correct (fails closed, no loss, blocks the runbook section 6 canary).

findings.lens: FWA core, parity and liability conservation (HyperEVM mainne
findings.title: One-shot setRewards can be blocked forever by a 0.01-HYPE deposit if the Safe executes the activation batch before preActivation
findings.lines: PrepareMainnetOwnerActions.ps1:28-52 and 79-84 (ordering is a JSON note only); FWA.sol:2347-2358 (setRewards), 804-878 (_createListing), 1056-1083 (withdrawListing)
findings.preconditions: The owner Safe executes `activationBatch` (whitelist collections + `ACQUISITIONS_ENABLED = true`) before `preActivation` (`FWA.setRewards`). Nothing on chain enforces the order for the Safe path; the ordering exists only as free text in the generated JSON's `notes` array and as a precondition check inside the alternative forge scripts.
findings.scenario: Safe executes `whitelist.setCollections([C1…Cn], true)`. An adversary immediately calls `listNFT{value: 0.01 ether}(C1, tokenId)` with any token from a now-allowlisted collection — the minimum backing is 0.01 HYPE (FWA.sol:331), so the attack costs cents. `activeListingCount` becomes 1. The Safe then submits `preActivation`, and `setRewards` reverts on `if (activeListingCount != 0 || stagedCount != 0 || reservedStagedCount != 0) revert InvalidConfig()` (FWA.sol:2350). The adversary simply never calls `withdrawListing`; only the depositor can withdraw, and the owner has no force-exit. `setBool(WITHDRAW_ONLY, true)` stops new deposits but cannot remove the existing one, and it simultaneously blocks acquisitions (`_validateAcquisition`, FWA.sol:1356), so the listing can no longer be allocated out either.
findings.impact: `setRewards` is a strictly one-shot setter (`if (address(rewards) != address(0)) revert InvalidConfig()`), so the entire FWAToken rewards/emission/`acceptBidAsTokens` leg becomes permanently unattachable to this core. Recovery is possible but costly and economically wrong: de-whitelist every collection, open acquisitions with no rewards module bound, buy out the griefing listing yourself, settle it, then bind rewards — meaning all early acquisitions run with no `registerAcquisition` epoch and no token slice, permanently distorting the reward accounting the manifest promises.
findings.minimalFix: Make the ordering an on-chain invariant rather than a note: emit the Safe batch as a single MultiSend whose first call is `setRewards`, or have `PrepareMainnetOwnerActions.ps1` refuse to emit `activationBatch` unless `FWA.rewards()` already reads non-zero on chain (it already has `cast` available). Mirroring the `BindNestRewards.s.sol:48-53` `CoreNotReady` check into the JSON generator is the minimal change.
findings.regressionTest: `testSetRewardsCannotBeGriefedByADustDeposit`: whitelist a collection, have a non-owner deposit at `minBacking`, then assert `setRewards` reverts — and assert that the release tooling refuses to emit an activation batch in that state.

refutationNotes.reason: SURVIVES AT MEDIUM, ONE PREMISE IS FACTUALLY WRONG. The mechanism checks out: _createListing (FWA.sol:804-878) gates only on withdrawOnly, minBacking, code.length and collectionWhitelisted - it does NOT require acquisitionsEnabled - so the griefing window opens at activationBatch item 1 (whitelist.setCollections) even if item 2 is never executed. setRewards (2347-2358) then reverts on activeListingCount != 0 and is strictly one-shot, only the depositor can withdrawListing, and setBool(WITHDRAW_ONLY) cannot evict an existing listing while also blocking the acquisition path (_validateAcquisition, 1356). The mainnet FWAWhitelist is constructed with ttt = address(0) so the burn path is disabled, confirming the owner Safe is the only opener. HOWEVER the claim that 'the ordering exists only as free text in the generated JSON notes array' is wrong: MAINNET_RELEASE_RUNBOOK_2026-07-26.md section 4.4 mandates it in the body ('Executer d'abord uniquement preActivation... Le pool NFT doit etre vide'), the JSON carries explicit order:1/order:2 fields on the activation entries, and the forge alternative ActivateHyperEVMMainnet.s.sol:73 hard-reverts InvalidWiring when address(fwa.rewards()) != address(rewards). So the gap is narrower than presented - it is the Safe path lacking the on-chain generator guard that the forge path already has. Severity medium still fits 'recoverable griefing' (recovery via de-whitelist, buy out, settle, bind), and the proposed fix - have PrepareMainnetOwnerActions.ps1 refuse to emit activationBatch unless cast reports fwa.rewards() non-zero - is correct and cheap. Keep at medium with the premise corrected.

Verified end to end. FWA.sol:2347-2350 makes setRewards one-shot AND conditional on activeListingCount == 0 && stagedCount == 0 && reservedStagedCount == 0; FWA.sol:331 sets minBacking to 0.01 ether; _createListing (804-878) admits any non-owner deposit of a whitelisted collection while acquisitionsEnabled is still false; withdrawListing (1056-1083) is depositor-only via _activeOwned (1050-1054) and there is no owner force-exit anywhere in the contract. My probe confirms setRewards reverts InvalidConfig after a single 0.01 ether deposit by a non-owner. The ordering really is off-chain only on the Safe path: PrepareMainnetOwnerActions.ps1:28-52 emits preActivation and activationBatch as independent payloads whose sequencing exists solely as free text in the notes array (79-84) and in runbook line 85; the on-chain equivalent guard exists only in the alternative forge path (ActivateHyperEVMMainnet.s.sol:73 checks address(fwa.rewards()) != address(rewards) -> InvalidWiring), which the Safe route bypasses entirely. This is squarely the 'a gate off-chain does not replace an on-chain invariant' class.

One correction to the recovery analysis, which does not change the severity: the finding proposes setBool(WITHDRAW_ONLY, true) and then notes it also blocks acquisitions. The cheaper recovery is setCollectionsWhitelisted(collections, false) (FWA.sol:2338-2344), which stops NEW deposits without touching the acquisition path, after which the griefing listing can be acquired out and setRewards bound. Absent that, the griefer can re-deposit on every attempt, so the on-chain fix in the finding is still warranted. Severity medium (recoverable griefing on a one-shot setter) is correct.

findings.lens: FWA core, parity and liability conservation (HyperEVM mainne
findings.title: An unfulfillable randomness request pins pendingRequestCount and unfulfilledVrfCount forever, locking VRF reconfiguration, coordinator migration and the coordinator reserve
findings.preconditions: A request is issued and its Gelato fulfilment never lands — the task is deleted or paused, the Gas Tank empties, the targeted drand round is missed, or the consumer callback reverts persistently (e.g. FWA's coordinator pointer was already changed, so `rawFulfillRandomWords` reverts `OnlyCoordinator` and `fulfillRandomness` reverts `ConsumerCallbackFailed`, line 165).
findings.scenario: `requestRandomWords` increments `pendingRequestCount` (line 129) and FWA increments `unfulfilledVrfCount` (FWA.sol:1418). The only decrement path in the coordinator is a successful `fulfillRandomness` (line 158); there is no expiry, cancel or owner override. FWA's local expiry deliberately does not decrement `unfulfilledVrfCount` (FWA.sol:250-253), and `reconcileUnfulfilledVrfCount` fails closed on `pendingRequestExists` (FWA.sol:1466), which for this coordinator is exactly `pendingRequestCount != 0`. The state is therefore permanently non-zero, and it is self-reinforcing with the deadlock: `setAddr(VRF_COORDINATOR, …)` requires `unfulfilledVrfCount == 0` (FWA.sol:2324), so you cannot migrate away from the coordinator whose stuck request is the reason you want to migrate.
findings.impact: Permanently blocks `setUint(VRF_SUB_ID)`, `setAddr(VRF_COORDINATOR)` and `FWAVRFService.setVrfRequestConfig` → `FWA.configureVrfRequest` (gas lane / callback-gas changes). `GelatoVRFCoordinator.withdrawNative` is blocked too (line 208), stranding the accumulated purchaser-funded reserve. And `requiredSubscriptionBalance` is permanently inflated by `maxFulfillmentCostWei` per stuck request, so each one permanently consumes 0.01 HYPE of the service's liquid balance as coverage; enough stuck requests make `prepareRequests` revert `InsufficientVrfCoverage` and halt all acquisitions until the owner tops the service up.
findings.minimalFix: Add an owner-only (or timelocked, deadline-gated) `abandonRequest(uint256 requestId)` on `GelatoVRFCoordinator` that may only run after the request is provably past FWA's word deadline, sets `status = Fulfilled` without calling the consumer, and decrements `pendingRequestCount`. Pair it with a runbook step that calls `FWA.reconcileUnfulfilledVrfCount()` afterwards so the two counters converge.
findings.regressionTest: `testStuckRequestCanBeRetiredAndCountersConverge`: issue a request, never fulfil it, roll past `wordDeadlineBlock`, run `processAcquisitions` to expire it, then assert `reconcileUnfulfilledVrfCount()` succeeds and `setAddr(VRF_COORDINATOR, newCoordinator)` no longer reverts `AcquisitionStateLocked`.

refutationNotes.reason:
The mechanics are accurate. GelatoVRFCoordinator.sol decrements pendingRequestCount only at line 158 inside a successful fulfillRandomness; there is no expiry, cancel or owner override, and withdrawNative (206-213) is gated on pendingRequestCount == 0. FWA's local expiry deliberately leaves unfulfilledVrfCount untouched (comment 250-253, code 1505-1510), and reconcileUnfulfilledVrfCount (1463-1469) fails closed on pendingRequestExists, which for this coordinator is literally pendingRequestCount != 0 (line 180-183). setUint(VRF_SUB_ID) (2238), setAddr(VRF_COORDINATOR) (2324) and configureVrfRequest (1447) all require unfulfilledVrfCount == 0, so the described deadlock is a genuine code property.

Severity is overstated. fulfillRandomness carries NO deadline of its own - it validates only status, round, consumer, callbackGasLimit and payload hash (147-152). drand beacons for a past round remain permanently retrievable, so every plausible trigger the finding lists (task paused, task deleted and recreated, Gas Tank emptied, round missed) is recoverable by restoring the Gelato task and submitting the late beacon: the coordinator decrements pendingRequestCount, FWA's callbackObserved branch (1493-1497) decrements unfulfilledVrfCount, and both counters converge without any new code. Only a permanently dead OPERATOR key makes it terminal, which is a tail scenario. Meanwhile nothing user-facing is blocked: new acquisitions, settlement, refunds, exits and every pull path keep working; the stranded amount is the coordinator's compatibility reserve, on the order of minimumSubscriptionBuffer + n*maxFulfillmentCost (~0.02 HYPE), i.e. protocol funds not user funds; and the 'halts all acquisitions' escalation is always clearable by sending HYPE to the service's permissionless receive() (FWAVRFService.sol:154-156). No user fund impact, fails closed, narrow trigger, recoverable in the common cases: correct severity is low (hardening / recovery-path gap), not medium.

findings.title: The FWAVRFService coverage invariant is semantically void under Gelato: it underwrites a balance nothing spends while the real fulfilment budget has no on-chain gate, so purchasers pay the randomness fee for randomness that is never delivered
findings.preconditions: Gelato Gas Tank / 1Balance exhausted or the VRF task paused, while `ACQUISITIONS_ENABLED` is true on 999.
findings.scenario: The coordinator's own comment at line 197 states it: 'Compatibility reserve used by FWAVRFService; Gelato execution is funded separately in Gas Tank.' `nativeSubscriptionBalance` is only ever increased by `fundSubscriptionWithNative` and decreased by owner `withdrawNative` — no fulfilment path debits it. FWA's only on-chain brake on issuing new requests is `FWAVRFService.prepareRequests -> _ensureSubscriptionCoverage`, which reverts `InsufficientVrfCoverage` when the coordinator's balance cannot be topped up to `minimumSubscriptionBuffer + (unfulfilledVrfCount + n) * maxFulfillmentCostWei`. Since the coordinator's balance never falls, that gate is permanently satisfied once funded and can never observe the real failure. Ordering: (1) Gas Tank hits zero at block N; nothing on-chain changes. (2) Purchasers keep calling `acquire`, each paying `acquisitionFee + vrfServiceFee` where `vrfServiceFee = 800_000 * tx.gasprice * 1.3` (.env.mainnet.example:30-31 / FWAVRFService.sol:191-193); the VRF slice is forwarded into FWAVRFService and never returned. (3) 30 blocks later `processAcquisitions` takes the Pending branch (FWA.sol:1559-1565) and `_creditAcquisitionRefund` (FWA.sol:1584-1591) credits back ONLY `acquisition.priceEscrowed`. (4) Each such request also increments `pendingRequestCount` permanently (see the no-expiry finding), so the outage compounds into a permanent coordinator lock.
findings.impact: Every purchaser during a Gas Tank outage permanently loses the randomness service fee for a draw that never happened, with no on-chain circuit breaker and no user-visible signal; the acquisition fee is refunded but the randomness fee is not. The entire `unfulfilledVrfCount` / `requiredSubscriptionBalance` / `InsufficientVrfCoverage` machinery inherited from the Ethereum deployment — where Chainlink actually debits the subscription — is a no-op on HyperEVM: a safety invariant ported syntactically but not semantically. Accounting is not insolvent, but the gate designed to fail closed fails open.
findings.minimalFix: Enforce liveness where it is observable: in `GelatoVRFCoordinator.requestRandomWords`, revert new requests while a stale pending request exists, e.g. track `oldestPendingBlock` and `if (oldestPendingBlock != 0 && block.number > oldestPendingBlock + STALL_BLOCKS) revert RandomnessStalled();` with `STALL_BLOCKS` a small multiple of FWA's `selectionTimeoutBlocks`. This needs no change to the verified core and turns a silent fee drain into a clean revert. Complementarily, either refund the randomness fee on expiry, or stop advertising it as a fee 'paid to the provider before the request' (frontend/src/components/docs/docsContent.tsx:259) when on 999 the provider is paid off-chain.
findings.regressionTest: `testAcquisitionsHaltWhenFulfilmentStalls`: fund the service, acquire, never fulfil, `vm.roll` past STALL_BLOCKS, then assert the next `pool.acquire{value:...}` reverts (`RandomnessStalled`) instead of accepting and burning another randomness fee; and assert the purchaser of the stalled request recovers `priceEscrowed` via `withdrawAcquisitionRefund` while `pendingRequestExists` is cleared by `expireRequest`.

refutationNotes.reason: The core observation SURVIVES but the framing contains one inherited-behaviour error and one factual error; correct severity is low. TRUE and verified: nativeSubscriptionBalance is only ever increased by fundSubscriptionWithNative (198-204) and decreased by owner withdrawNative (206-213) — no fulfilment path debits it — so once _ensureSubscriptionCoverage (FWAVRFService.sol:242-255) has funded it, `current >= required` holds forever and InsufficientVrfCoverage can never observe a Gelato funding failure. That is a genuine semantic no-op versus Chainlink and there is indeed no on-chain brake tied to Gelato liveness. NOT a port defect: the non-refund of vrfServiceFee on expiry is inherited byte-for-byte from the verified Ethereum reference — _creditAcquisitionRefund (FWA.sol:1584-1592) refunds only priceEscrowed there too, and the fee is not lost value but stays in FWAVRFService as processor-reimbursement surplus (availableProcessorSurplus, 225-235). Presenting parity-preserved reference behaviour as a HyperEVM defect is the kind of finding the mandate explicitly excludes. FACTUALLY WRONG: step (4), 'each such request also increments pendingRequestCount permanently, so the outage compounds into a permanent coordinator lock' — a fulfilment delivered after the Gas Tank is refilled decrements it and is accepted by FWA without reverting (FWA.sol:1493-1502), so a Gas-Tank outage does not compound. The UX half is also wrong: docsContent.tsx:259 says the randomness fee is 'paid to the provider before the request', which is literally accurate on 999 — it is paid to FWAVRFService via prepareRequests{value: vrf} before requestRandomWords (FWA.sol:1284). Residual actionable issue = no on-chain liveness circuit-breaker: low.

THE OBSERVATION IS CORRECT BUT THE IMPACT AND THE CATEGORY ARE BOTH OVERSTATED. Verified: `nativeSubscriptionBalance` is only credited by `fundSubscriptionWithNative` (198-204) and debited by owner `withdrawNative` (206-213); no fulfilment path touches it; the coordinator says so itself at line 197. So `_ensureSubscriptionCoverage` (FWAVRFService.sol:242-255) can never observe a Gas Tank outage and `InsufficientVrfCoverage` cannot fire for that cause. Recording that the ported coverage machinery is a no-op on HyperEVM is fair. What does not hold: (1) the magnitude — the unrefunded slice is `800_000 * tx.gasprice * 1.3` (FWAVRFService.sol:191-193), roughly 1e-4 HYPE at 0.1 gwei, and it is not destroyed, it stays in FWAVRFService as owner-withdrawable surplus; (2) 'contract-bug' is the wrong category, since the coordinator behaves exactly as its own documented contract states and the FWAVRFService/FWA code is the unmodified verified Ethereum reference; (3) the non-refund of the randomness fee on expiry is inherited, not a port defect — `_creditAcquisitionRefund` (FWA.sol:1584-1591) refunds only `priceEscrowed` on Ethereum too; (4) real fail-safes do exist — every stalled acquisition expires after `selectionTimeoutBlocks` and fully refunds the pool fee, and the owner can flip ACQUISITIONS_ENABLED or WITHDRAW_ONLY; (5) the 'compounds into a permanent coordinator lock' tail depends entirely on finding #2, which I downgraded. Low, as hardening/telemetry: a stall detector in the coordinator would be a genuine improvement.

findings.title: Mainnet activation opens public acquisitions before any on-chain evidence that the Gelato operator can fulfil; both randomness gates are unverifiable env booleans and the canary runs after the open
findings.preconditions: Mainnet activation run by the owner Safe/key. The Gelato task not actually created, mis-bound to the wrong contract, or the Gas Tank empty, while the two env flags have been set to true.
findings.scenario: The only checks tying activation to a working randomness source are `vm.envBool("GELATO_VRF_TASK_CONFIRMED")` (line 44) and `vm.envBool("GELATO_GAS_TANK_FUNDED_CONFIRMED")` (line 45) — plain environment variables with no on-chain counterpart, defaulted to false in .env.mainnet.example:11-12. The one related on-chain assertion is `coordinator.pendingRequestCount() != 0` (line 68), which passes trivially when `requestCount == 0`, so 'never used' and 'proven working' are indistinguishable to the script. `whitelist.setCollections(collections, true)` and `fwa.setBool(ACQUISITIONS_ENABLED, true)` are in the same broadcast (79-80), so there is no restricted-collection canary window. The runbook's own sequence confirms the ordering: 'L'activation on-chain ouvre une fenêtre de canary' (line 56) — the canary happens AFTER the public open, and `MAINNET_E2E_CONFIRMED` (line 58) only gates `PromoteMainnetManifest.ps1`, i.e. the frontend. Between the open and the canary the contract is live to anyone reading the chain or the indexer; the only thing keeping users away is that the website has not been promoted.
findings.impact: If the Gelato wiring is wrong, the failure is discovered with public money already at risk: every acquisition in that window loses its randomness fee (see the coverage finding) and permanently increments `pendingRequestCount` (see the no-expiry finding), which is irreversible. The mandate's rule applies exactly — a safety property whose only enforcement is a human-set boolean, with an irreversible consequence.
findings.minimalFix: Make the gate on-chain and put the canary before the open. (1) Split the script: step A enables acquisitions with `FWA_COLLECTIONS` set to a team-controlled collection only; step B, after a real end-to-end fulfilment, adds the public collections. (2) In step B require positive on-chain proof that the real operator fulfilled at least once: `if (coordinator.requestCount() == 0 || coordinator.pendingRequestCount() != 0 || coordinator.fulfilledWord(1) == 0) revert RandomnessNotProven();`. (3) Keep the env booleans as an additional human gate, never as the only one.
findings.regressionTest: Add a Foundry script self-test under release/script-self-test that forks/simulates 999 state and asserts `ActivateHyperEVMMainnet.run()` reverts `RandomnessNotProven` when the coordinator has `requestCount() == 0`, and succeeds only after a simulated operator fulfilment of request 1.

refutationNotes.reason: SURVIVES as hardening; medium is overstated because the load-bearing 'irreversible open' premise is false. Facts verified: ActivateHyperEVMMainnet.s.sol:44-45 gates only on vm.envBool(GELATO_VRF_TASK_CONFIRMED) and vm.envBool(GELATO_GAS_TANK_FUNDED_CONFIRMED), both defaulted false at .env.mainnet.example:11-12; line 68's `coordinator.pendingRequestCount() != 0` is a no-in-flight check that indeed cannot distinguish 'never used' from 'proven working'; lines 79-80 whitelist collections and set ACQUISITIONS_ENABLED in one broadcast; the runbook puts the canary after (DRAND_GELATO_RANDOMNESS_RUNBOOK.md:56). But the mandate's rule the finding invokes applies to IRREVERSIBLE opens, and this open is trivially reversible: FWA.setBool (2295-2312) has no acquisition-state lock at all, so ACQUISITIONS_ENABLED can be flipped back in one owner transaction — which is precisely what runbook line 56 already prescribes. Value at risk in the canary window is also near zero: collections are whitelisted in the same transaction, so the pool starts empty and _validateAcquisition reverts NoActiveListings while totalWeight==0 (FWA.sol:1358); a third party must first deposit an NFT before anyone can acquire. Finally, the recommended two-step canary needs no script change — the operator can run the same script once with a team-only FWA_COLLECTIONS and again with the public list, since setCollections is additive. The residual value is the proposed on-chain proof-of-fulfilment precondition (requestCount()>0 && fulfilledWord(1)!=0): worthwhile defence in depth, low.

SURVIVES ONLY AS PROCESS HARDENING; THE 'irreversible' FRAMING IS REFUTED. Facts confirmed: ActivateHyperEVMMainnet.s.sol:44-45 are plain `vm.envBool` flags; `coordinator.pendingRequestCount() != 0` (68) is trivially satisfied at zero; `setCollections` and `setBool(ACQUISITIONS_ENABLED,true)` are in one broadcast (79-80); DRAND_GELATO_RANDOMNESS_RUNBOOK.md:56 does place the canary after the on-chain open. But the script is not purely env-gated — line 65-76 asserts fifteen-plus on-chain wiring invariants including `coordinator.OPERATOR() == expectedOperator` AND `expectedOperator.code.length != 0`, i.e. that the configured dedicated sender is a live contract on 999. More importantly the open is fully REVERSIBLE: `setBool(ACQUISITIONS_ENABLED,false)` and `setCollectionsWhitelisted(..., false)` (FWA.sol:2302-2303, 2338-2344) both exist and the runbook already instructs exactly that rollback ('refermer immédiatement ACQUISITIONS_ENABLED via le Safe'). The canary-first split the finding demands is already achievable with the shipped script, since `FWA_COLLECTIONS` is operator-chosen and `setCollections` is additive: whitelist a team-only collection, canary, re-run with the public list. With no whitelisted collection there is nothing to deposit and `acquire` reverts `NoActiveListings` (FWA.sol:1358), so the window is not automatically live. And if the Gelato wiring is wrong the worst case is expiry plus a full pool-fee refund; only the ~1e-4 HYPE randomness fee is at risk, so 'public money already at risk' is a large overstatement. The mandate's 'a gate off-chain does not replace an on-chain invariant' rule applies, but its consequence clause ('when the consequence is loss of funds or an irreversible open') is not met here.

findings.title: Live frontend cannot reach most of the 300M FWA reward program: withdrawTokens/claimAccruedTokens absent from the ABI and claimableEpochs hard-coded empty
findings.preconditions: NEXT_PUBLIC_DATA_MODE=mainnet with the rewards module deployed and emitting.
findings.scenario: fwaRewardsAbi (abi.ts:314-368) exposes only two writes — claimDepositorTokens and claimEpochTokens — and no `tokenCredit`, `withdrawTokens`, `claimAccruedTokens`, `withdrawTokenBuyAllowanceAsETH`, `purchaserEpochAmount`, `userAcquisitionsInEpoch`, `purchaserClaimed`, or `pendingAcquisitionsInEpoch` reads. Consequences, all on mainnet: (1) When a listing is repriced or removed — which is the normal end state, since FWA.onListingRemoved fires on every acquisition — FWARewardsHyperEVM._creditPending (lines 411-417) moves the depositor's accrued FWA out of the per-listing accumulator and into tokenCredit[depositor], claimable only via withdrawTokens(). getRewards only sums pendingDepositorTokens over listings that are still `status === "active"` (lines 921-936), so a depositor whose NFT was acquired sees 0 and the app offers no way to withdraw. (2) getRewards returns `purchaserClaimable: 0n` and `claimableEpochs: []` as literals (lines 966-967), so the "Claim epoch FWA" button is permanently disabled (RewardsScreen.tsx:180) — the entire 150M purchaser epoch program is unreachable through the product. (3) The screen renders "Accrued via token settlements" from tokenBuyAllowance (RewardsScreen.tsx:171) but there is no claimAccruedTokens write anywhere, so that balance is displayed as if claimable and cannot be spent. Meanwhile FWARewardsHyperEVM.rescueTokens (lines 623-633) lets the owner drain the module's whole FWA balance once the core is in withdrawOnly.
findings.impact: The majority of the 300M FWA reward budget is invisible and unclaimable through the shipped product, while the UI presents balances as claimable. Users must hand-craft contract calls to recover value the app told them they had.
findings.minimalFix: Add tokenCredit(address), purchaserEpochAmount(uint256), userAcquisitionsInEpoch(uint256,address), purchaserClaimed(uint256,address), pendingAcquisitionsInEpoch(uint256) reads and withdrawTokens()/claimAccruedTokens(uint256) writes to fwaRewardsAbi; compute claimableEpochs by scanning epochs [0, currentEpoch) for userAcquisitionsInEpoch > 0 && !purchaserClaimed && pendingAcquisitionsInEpoch == 0; sum depositorPending as pendingDepositorTokens(active listings) + tokenCredit(account); and expose a distinct "spend allowance" action wired to claimAccruedTokens with a user-set minOut.
findings.regressionTest: Frontend integration test against an anvil fork: activate a listing, accrue emission, remove the listing, and assert the client reports the tokenCredit balance and that a withdrawTokens transaction is offered; settle an acquisition, advance past the epoch boundary, and assert claimableEpochs is non-empty and the claim succeeds.

refutationNotes.reason:
SURVIVES — fully verified, and it is contradicted by the project's own documentation, so it is not a disclosed limit.

fwaRewardsAbi (frontend/src/protocol/viem/abi.ts:314-368) contains exactly two writes, claimDepositorTokens and claimEpochTokens, and no tokenCredit / withdrawTokens / claimAccruedTokens / withdrawTokenBuyAllowanceAsETH / purchaserEpochAmount / userAcquisitionsInEpoch / purchaserClaimed / pendingAcquisitionsInEpoch. A repo-wide grep for claimAccruedTokens, withdrawTokens and tokenCredit across frontend/src returns ZERO hits — they exist nowhere in the product. ViemProtocolClient.ts:964-967 returns `purchaserClaimable: 0n` and `claimableEpochs: []` as literals, while the mock engine (mock/engine.ts:339-342, fixtures.ts:428-431) populates both — so the screen is exercised only in mock mode. RewardsScreen.tsx:180 gates the button on `(user?.purchaserClaimable ?? 0n) <= 0n`, i.e. permanently disabled on mainnet. The _creditPending path (FWARewardsHyperEVM.sol:411-417) is confirmed to move accrual into tokenCredit on every reprice/removal, and ViemProtocolClient.ts:921-936 sums pendingDepositorTokens over status === 'active' listings only, so a depositor whose NFT was acquired sees 0 with no withdrawal offered. frontend/INTEGRATION_NEEDS.md:8 asserts 'claims' are ready in code and lists only external addresses/services as outstanding — the doc is wrong.

(Adjacent, same root cause and worth folding in: getPositions.deposited at ViemProtocolClient.ts:874 includes `staged` listings, and claimDepositorTokens reverts ListingNotActive on any non-active id, so the depositor button can revert too.)

Severity medium -> low strictly by the supplied rubric. No fund impact: the contract entry points are permissionless and directly callable, nothing is lost or locked, and the UI understates rather than overstates a balance. That is textbook 'misleading UI with no fund impact' = low. It sits at the top of the low band and should still be a launch blocker on product-completeness grounds — but it is not medium.

findings.title: Closed-market buy gate is keyed on the swap recipient, so any outsider can trade the "closed" pool
findings.preconditions: Market launched (launched == true), externalBuysEnabled == false — i.e. the entire bootstrap window the runbook describes as "achats publics contrôlés uniquement par setExternalBuysEnabled" (NEST_DEPLOYMENT_RUNBOOK.md:17-18).
